Title: A common future for three continents?
text: A COMMON FUTURE FOR THREE CONTINENTS? Kicmelt temak John Plender might be right in ruling out the Japanification for America and the EU /Ft, 23/24 May 2020/. Indeed, due to a couple of reasons - to combat the effects of the Covid-19 pandemic, to save the social structures in America and Europe, to maintain the fragile balance between the Northern and Southern members of the Eurozone governments and central banks will use fiscal and monetaiy pumps heavily. It will result in higher inflation rates and much higher public debts. Finally, central banks will be forced to raise interest rates and governments will return to austerity policies. It will be unbearable politically, so the next step might be a one-tier banking system, the abolition of former public debts and a brand-new financial system based on digital central bank money, gold and electricity. It might mean a new Bretton Woods Agreement or/and a new Plaza Agreement. It might work without huge public debts and risks of runaway inflation The same future for Japan, the US and Europe as well? Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Fears of Japanification spreading are misplaced

Title: A lifetime opportunity to buy bargains
text: A LIFETIME OPPORTUNITY TO BUY BARGAINS Kicmelt temak John Rogers, one of the most successful asset managers, an African American, suggests being a little bit contrarian, being a kind of a fish out of water in order to win /FT, 5 April 2021/ Indeed, we all need a realty rich environment to leam how to think independently and to believe in rigorous inquiry and debate. It is especially true of the new investors of our emerging economies in Central Europe where the present crisis offers a once-in-a-lifetime business opportunity for all contrarians. New start-ups, fest growing SMEs, internet-based new services, new technologies, even newly listed SE companies deserve our time and money. To be a contrarian or not to be at all, this is the question Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Taking a contrarian view to beat markets and prejudice

Title: A new cycle has just begun
text: A NEW CYCLE HAS JUST BEGUN Kicmelt temak Indeed, ministers and health officials are far more important for the economy now, than central bankers. /Chris Giles, FT, 2 October/ In the 2010s, the banking sector was the key player in the global economy. However, lack of proper financial regulation led to the global financial crisis in 2007/2009. Of course, central bankers solved the crisis, because it was a full-fledged financial crisis. This time it is different, the present crisis is a mixture of a pandemic, fear and all sorts of challenges to sustainability. To solve it, we need the right policies of realty efficient, creative and able governments. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Central bankers have been relegated to second division of policymakers

Title: A new deal for all of us
text: ANEW DEAL FOR ALL OF US Kicmelt temak All of us, young, middle-aged and elders, definitely need a new deal Actually, we need tailor-made new deals to fix the present and especially the looming housing, health, job and other crises. /FT, Editorial, 26 April 2021/ This is due to the very nature of todays sea-changes in all high-income societies and also in emerging economies. While we have the same challenges - health issues, security, affordability of housing, climate change, jobs, access to outstanding education and flexibility to change homes and professions - for all generations, where the solutions differ for the different age groups. No one can solve one of them without solving the others: they are intertwined. Elderly people need much better, sustainable, green housing with plenty of smart health-care facilities. Middle-aged active generations need much more new homes in order to follow job opportunities and changes in the size of the family. Young generations need bubbly city life and brilliant universities to attend, so they should have access to a plenty of affordable rents. New and green housing programs should embrace all kinds of tailor-made new deals in order to build many new sustainable homes and to renovate old ones. These new deals can merge housing, health-care, job creation, education and the fight against climate change. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central bank of Hungary Re A new deal for the young: how to fix the housing crisis

Title: A new global landscape
text: A NEW GLOBAL LANDSCAPE Kicmelt temak On the one hand the source of political risk and instability is indeed shifting between developed and emerging markets /Gillian Tett, FT, 2 October 2020/, but on the other hand we witness the emergence of two new groups of countries. The first one tends to be a northern economy, with able governments, enlightened population and strong institutions. The second one tends to be a southern economy, with weak governments, divided population and decentralized institutions. There are exceptions to the rule, especially when a northern developed countiy does not enjoy the benefits of an able government. This is a new geography for investors where the effectiveness of governments and central banks determine the results of handling both the pandemic and the future reconstruction of the economy. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Investors grapple with a bizarre US election cycle

Title: A new power law
text: A NEW POWER LAW Kicmelt temak All sincere and sober voices are more than welcomed with regard to the US. initiated America-China tensions - John Plender did his best by sending out the right noises. /Market Insights, FT, 3 Novenber 2020/ He is right that the Chinese government bond market, the second largest in the world, offers positive real interest income after allowing for inflation It means that developed countries pension funds can benefit from real incomes and they are able to pay retirement obligations. This is also true for all western institutional investors as well By now it is clear, that who decides to hurt China also hurts itself Indeed, by bashing Beijing the U.S. suffered more than China. That is the new power law in our global hut. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Chinese economy outstrips US despite Beijing bashing

Title: A rerun of Bretton Woods might be coming
text: A RERUN OF BRETTON WOODS MIGHT BE COMING Kicmelt temak The fight between cryptocurrcncics and central banks has just begun /Katie Martin, FT, 22 May/23 May 2021/ In 1944/1945 a new global financial system was bom and served well the world economy over a 26/27-y period. In 1971 it was abolished by the US President. In the aftermath of Nixons decision currency wars and financial warfare replaced stability in international money markets. In 1996, after 25 years, the internet stepped in and a long period of transition started in the financial world. Around 2000 the euro entered the scene as a game-changer. The global financial crisis in 2008 and the euro zone crisis in 2010/12 reignited financial instabilities. Ciyptocurrencies started to rise as safe-heavens based on new internet-based technologies. Fintech sectors, ciyptocurrencies, the America-China standoff and the Covid-19 pandemic are intertwined with each other. By now, all players ciy for a new global financial order. After 25/26 years it might be coming soon. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Cryptocurrency holders take on central banks at their peril

Title: A second chance for Europe
text: A SECOND CHANCE FOR EUROPE Kicmelt temak Martin Sandbu warns the EU not to repeat the mistakes of the 201 Os in policy-making, when European leaders shifted from stimulus to tightening / FT, 12 August 2020/. However, this time it is not enough for the EU to suspend the fiscal rules to avoid repeating the mistakes, made a decade ago, because we missed exactly a decade to free and soke the real European challenges. The crisis gives us a chance to free the crisis of demography, migration, the euro, global competitiveness, long-term sustainability across the board, healthcare systems, political stalemates within the EU, wealth creation and job creation Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re  Europe risks another false dawn after coronavirus

Title: A wartime targeted stimulus programme is needed
text: A WARTIME TARGETED STIMULUS PROGRAMME IS NEEDED Kicmelt temak Rana Foroohar is absolutely right that we should not mistake all the money currently offered by governments and central banks for a cure / FT, 16 March 2020/. Indeed, we need a wartime stimulus programme that compensates for the loss of private-sector spending. She is also right that we need a major public health spending programme. Yes, we badly need targeted means to boost demand and restore trust in our economies. Targeting public health spending and reforming the entire health-care system is definitely right, in more than one way. The coronavirus has singled out elderly people. They need better protection against present and future attacks Also, our societies are greying fast, and we need better means to fight against the losses coming with ageing. Re How the virus became a credit run Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: All is well that ends well
text: ALL IS WELL THAT ENDS WELL Kicmelt temak Of course histoiy will judge how nations fared over the full course of the pandemic /Ruchir Shanna, FT, 24 May 2021/. However, all the successes and failures of the fight against the pandemic will remain with us and all countries have lessons to learn from the pandemic. The single most important lesson to be learnt from this pandemic is that self correction, changing courses fest, evaluating mistakes and avoiding complacency proved to be instrumental to the final success. These virtues, or the lack thereof were the main sources of both temporaiy wins and also momentary defeats. At the end of the day, all nations will win this war against the pandemic, fear and economic crisis. The time needed to win and the overall losses will determine the final ranking of the winners. This will be a useful tool for forecasting the rise and fell of nations. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re The short shelflife of pandemic national success stories

Title: Another kind of awkward truth
text: ANOTHER KIND OF AWKWARD TRUTH... Kicmclt temak In a veiy smart but biased - against the Germans - article /Philp Stephens, FT, 13 September 2019/ we spot Germany as the biggest beneficiaiy of European integration In the lack of European integration, we night find ourselves in German Europe, not as a present partner of a European Germany. It is urban legend, shared by even the Germans. I had the chance to listen to two German Chancellors repeating this nonsense. After WW 2, the Americans restructured Germany: there is only the European way for Germany in close alliance with the U.S. It is mandatoiy, not for choice. That is the reason why not only Germany, but also all other euro countries are required to boost consumption via much lower income taxes. Anyway, the original sin was not an untold truth, but the birth of a Western rival currency against the U.S. dollar. Re Germany, the euro and the awkward truth Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: At the end or the tailing end of it
text: AT THE END OR THE TAILING END OF IT Kicmelt temak We realty witness the ending of a long period of declining inflation, declining interest rates, and growing GDP, the perfect trifecta for all assets to do well /Margaret Franklin, FT, Monday 2 March 2020/. Indeed, it means that people are living for longer, with lower-for-longer returns and nobody practicing right now has any playbook for this. We might gain some insights from the 1940s and 1970s for the coming decade if we trust the hints of the cycles of histoiy. The gist of all these hints might be veiy simple: these years will be completely different from the previous decades. No outdated playbooks, please. RE: CFA chief on failing the worlds hardest exams Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Beware the Greeks bearing gifts
text: BEWARE THE GREEKS BEARING GIFTS Kicmelt temak The German proposal for an EU-wide insurance /Wolfgang Munchau, FT, 11 November 2019/ is indeed deceptive. In exchange for that they might request to get rid of all the tools that all others built to survive the harmful side-effects of the foiled economic policies of the EU in the last two decades. Some members used taxation to counter-balance the lack of independent monetaiy policies, others let their banks to load up with their home countrys government bonds without any risk weights, some others completely scrapped the criteria of the Maastricht Treaty. Without all these tools/tricks they could not survive the loss of their independent monetaiy policy, the austerity policies of the EU and the lack of a coordinated EU- wide fiscal and monetaiy policy. Both, the EU and the euro are half-baked institutions, you cannot improve them without fully-fledged reforms. Re Why the EU should be wary of Scholzs proposals Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Beyond GDP there is life
text: BEYOND GDP THERE IS LIFE Kicmelt temak It is certainty true that GDP-based measures are useful, clearly defined on one hand and unreliable, narrow-minded on the other hand. /James Sweeney, FT, 13 Januaiy 2021/ Nominal GDP is real GDP plus inflation, where both parts have a missing element. Nominal GDP fails to incorporate the real value of knowledge, at- home production, at-home services, free goods taken via the internet, all sorts of value-creation in family life from emotional intelligence to social behaviour. Inflation is also dubious due to the sweeping mega-trends behind economic and social changes. Digitalisation means that all the former knowledge of humankind becomes available for several billion people on earth - a huge value for free. It also means that all kinds of targeted knowledge are available for education, hardly calculable in terms of a lifetime income. GDP foils to measure the new fusion economy, where data is the most important resource for production When consumption becomes the most valuable foctor of production, all the others /capital, manpower, fossils and many more traditional foctors/ lose their value. We are still not good at measuring the transition from the old world to the world of fusions, so practically we cant measure inflation Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Why investors are looking beyond headline GDP data

Title: Both sides of the same coin
text: BOTH SIDES OF THE SAME COIN Kicmelt temak Mr Draghi was right a couple of weeks ago that fiscal policy should become the main instrument to stimulate demand /Martin Sandbu, FT, 18 September 2019/. He was also right to urge an explicit euro-level stance in 2014. His parting gift was aimed to use monetaiy policy on the other side of the same coin However, it is blatant that both sides of the coin are hostages of former political decisions. Fiscal policies are in the cage of the outgrown Stability and Growth Pact and the monetaiy policy of the ECB is in the cave of the outdated Maastricht Treaty. Both the fiscal policies of the eurozone countries and the monetaiy policies of the ECB should be rid of their chains. Re Eurozone wakes up to Draghis demand for fiscal stimulus Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Capital-heavy business models are back
text: CAPITAL-HEAVY BUSINESS MODELS ARE BACK Kicmelt temak Ian Harnett is mostly right telling us that the investment regime of the past two decades should be transformed /FT, 16 June 2021/. Indeed, capital-light businesses relied on globalization and the IT revolution Also, a Militaiy Civil Fusion did not seem imminent for a while. Nevertheless, investing in infrastructure and information is vital for governments and companies. Both are instrumental in winning the coming decades for all governments in the developed world and in the emerging economies. We badly need new fusions of government/central bank programs and new capital-heavy businesses to launch climate-transition technologies or deliver technological advances. Not either/or, both ways should be followed. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re "Put look is bright for capital-heavy business models

Title: Central banks need a new sustainability mandate
text: CENTRAL BANKS NEED A NEW SUSTAINABILITY MANDATE Kicmelt temak It is true that the worldwide fell in interest rates over the past two decades has caused a runaway boom in house prices; however, when demand for something rises, the only sane, logical response is to make more of it. /Robin Harding, FT, 7 April 2021/ I also fully agree with New Zealands rebelling central bank that does not consider the impact of housing when setting monetary policy. Nevertheless, to build more, larger and green homes we need both, free market response and targeted means from the state. We must create a completely new green market for housing via special government projects and targeted central banks programs. In order to complete the job, central banks need a new mandate to help all players who decide to contribute to a long-term sustainable economy. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Central banks should not target house prices

Title: Central banks will continue to act in isolation
text: CENTRAL BANKS WILL CONTINUE TO ACT IN ISOLATION Kicmelt temak According to a paper presented in Jackson Hole, the global long-run neutral level of central banks interest rates was pushed down by many global lactors. Some economists argue (Megan Greene, Financial Times, 30 August 2019) that when monetaiy policies diverge globally, they affect exchange rates, current accounts, credit flows and growth, and thus central banks can no longer afford to act in isolation On the contraiy, they can and will Fiscal policies will differ across countries, government policies will diverge, and all of this will result in diverging monetaiy policies by both major and smaller central banks. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the central bank of Hungary Re Central banks can no longer afford to act in isolation

Title: China is not a bubble, so it will not pop
text: CHINA IS NOT A BUBBLE, SO IT WILL NOT POP Kiemelt temak Chinas economic rise might be seen via bubbles; however, bubbles can persist when an economys growth rate consistently exceeds its interest rate. /Free exchange, The Economist Septenber 26th 2020/ It is not the case for China. Besides, in our near-zero interest rate world, bubbles will not occur as frequently as before. China has still plenty of room to lower interest rates when somewhat moderate growth rates replace historically sky-rocketing GDP growth figures. In addition to that, China proved to be extremely efficient in handling overheated parts of its economy via targeted monetaiy means. They will certainty repeat their success in the coming years, if needed. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re The mop that never stops

Title: Coming soon
text: COMING SOON... Kicmclt temak According to John Dizard, market freezes have a way of happening in March and September, an echo of the crop cycle. /FT, 20 Februaiy 2021/ Almost right, but not 100%. Let us include August because the majority of financial crises in the last 100 years emerged either in August or September. All the concerted efforts of the major players in the U.S. need more time to come up with a carefully crafted plan to create a new framework for global finances. They need a huge and constant flow of fresh dollar waves, higher but controlled inflation, new CBs digital currencies partly based on gold and a continuous depreciation of the dollar. There is no chance for a new Plaza Accord and a rerun of 1971 is also risky, so another plan might be on the way. Maybe in August or September, not in March Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Do not rule out a market panic next month

Title: Concerted efforts are needed
text: CONCERTED EFFORTS ARE NEEDED Kicmelt temak Evidently, for too long the eurozones banks have been a part of the problem, rather than a part of the solution/FT, 20 September 2019/. For sure, the ECB alone is not able to stimulate the economy. The QE programs helped to stabilize the eurozones financial systems but foiled to accelerate economic growth. Instead, all the major players should join their forces to do it. Fiscal policies should launch major overhauls of taxation by lowering all income taxes to enhance demand and raising some VAT-type taxes to stir up inflation, also to balance budgets. At the same time, the ECB should reduce equity capital requirements on all loans granted to the SME sector, green financing and digital transformation Re Eurozone banks need to be part of the solution Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Consumers are the only game in town
text: CONSUMERS ARE THE ONLY GAME IN TOWN Consumers are the only game in town 2019 CONSUMERS ARE THE ONLY GAME IN TOWN Kicmelt temak It is true that in the last 10 years global central banks were the only game in town It is also fair to say that the ECB is severely constrained in its ability to do more /Isabelle Mateos y Lago, FT, 5 Septenber 2019/. Indeed, the Eurozone needs a looser fiscal stance. Nevertheless, additional capital spending will not work, due to the two- in-one structure of the Eurozone. Stronger consumer spending is the only game in town. All members need a complete overhaul of taxation by lowering all income taxes that will temporarily- result in larger deficits. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the central bank of Hungary Re Tinkering with European fiscal rules will not be enough

Title: Coronavirus speeds up the rise of China
text: CORONAVIRUS SPEEDS UP THE RISE OF CHINA Kicmelt temak Rana Foroohar is definitely right that coronavirus has put a spotlight on the economic decoupling of China and some developed countries /FT, 24 February 2020/. Maybe it speeds up global decoupling. Maybe not. More likely it restructures global supply chains. More coupling might come in the no-virus, virtual economy - finance, research and development, culture, edutainment, creative economy- and more decoupling might occur in low tech, traditional sectors. The real change will happen to China inside, not in the global economy outside. China will recognize that the health industry is a vital part of the military strength of a nation. China will use its Al power to speed up breakthroughs in life sciences. They will also support the fusion of traditional Chinese and western medicine. Sub pondere crescit palma. Re Coronavirus speeds up global decoupling Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Covid is the first wake-up call for the West
text: COVID IS THE FIRST WAKE-UP CALL FOR THE WEST Kicmelt temak Just on the contraiy, there is no good reason to think that a healthy, ie. sustainable recoveiy is within reach in the western camp of the global economy. /Martin Wolf FT, 2 December 2020/ The handling of the Covid-19 pandemic might only be the harbinger of the handling of future challenges of the 2020s. The Asian pattern proved to be a success, the western pattern is a blatant failure. What realty matters in handling the coming challenges are the mindsets, habits and connections of the players from households to governments and from business sectors to civil movements. When it comes to wake-up calls double checking is the Asian way - lets expect some further calls. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re A light shines in the gloom cast by Covid-19

Title: Cycles of history matter a lot for Britain
text: CYCLES OF HISTORY MATTER A LOT FOR BRITAIN Kicmelt temak In a smart article, Philp Stephens argues for Realpolitik for post-Brexit Britain/FT, 20 December 2019/. Fully agreed, as for as foreign policy is concerned. Otherwise Britain can be the new global power in technology and finance. One can argue that both areas were covered by the EU member United Kingdom. Not at all, due to the more than comfortable position of Britain within the European Union. As for finance, London was the financial hub of the EU, no rivals and threats from inside. Regarding technology, services provided by the British business sector foced no rivals from inside, hence innovations in new industrial technologies were not pushed strong enough. Indeed, Britain seems to be again in 1940 /due to the 80ys cycle/, in 1970 /due to the 50ys cycle/ and in the 17th century /due to the rerun of the first 30ys war/. We cross our fingers for our friends. Re Realpolitik for post-Brexit Britain Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Debt is still debt
text: DEBT IS SHLLDEBT Kicmelt temak In a brave and smart article John Plender set the record straight: politicians have thrown caution to the wind by tailing to find alternative to fiscal expansion/FT, 1 July 2020/. May I put it bluntly: a lot of politicians in the developed world owe huge debts to their voters for not finding the right path to a sustainable future for the next generations. They regularly shied away from starting real structural reforms in order to improve the long-term sustainability of their economies. They might know that and feel guilty. It might be the real reason for piling up unmanageable budget deficits and public debts. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re What happens when asset prices are in the grp of central banks?

Title: Demography still plays a major role in the future
text: DEMOGRAPHY SHLL PLAYS A MAJOR ROLE IN THE FUTURE Kicmelt temak It is realty funny that in the western mindset there is only one solution to shrinking populations: mass migration. /Gideon Rachman, FT, 4 May 2021/ When it comes to China, they take for granted some kind of wishful thinking. Firstly, Chinas low fertility rate means that its population will shrink and age over the coming decades. Realty? What if China starts to heavily support families with two/three children in the coming decades? Secondly, China may never achieve the per-capita wealth levels of the US. Realty? What if China will pass the US per-capita wealth level well before the end of the 21th centuiy, meaning that it can maintain a generous pro- children strategy? It is true that demography will continue to shape world politics. This is the veiy reason why China will solve its demographic problems. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Lousy demographics will not stop Chinas rise

Title: Do not blame the Germans
text: DO NOT BLAME THE GERMANS... Kicmelt temak The globally leading, liberal weekly blames German prudence for the Eurozones woes (The Economist, 31 August 2019). It is realty funny that savings can become a sin instead of a virtue. They foil to admit that it is not Germanys savings, but the structure of the Eurozone that is to blame. There are two different Eurozones in one: the groups of Northern and Southern members. For the latter, new QE policies, negative rates and weaker exchange rates would be suitable. For the Northern countries, especially for Germany just the opposite is true. Prudence is realty dear when you have so much to lose. Re Dear prudence Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Do not play power politics
text: DO NOT PLAY POWER POLIHCS Kiemelt temak France indeed shows the signs of hyperactivity/Zaki Laidi, FT, 30 September 2019/ and some argue that Europe should stand on its two feet. Not again, please. The harmful dream of creating a United States of Europe is over, the euro zone is in shambles, the German economic machine and the French- German political engine both have come to a virtual standstill No surprise at all, because the EU tried to stand on its two feet, but tailed. Instead of a new adventure we badly need at least 27 nation states standing on their own feet, pursuing their tailor-made structural reforms in order to win their own future. The EU needs all the feet available to survive in the new G2 world. Re France seizes its moment on the world stage Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Do not stop worrying about public debt
text: DO NOT STOP WORRYING ABOUT PUBLIC DEBT Kiemelt temak Paul Krugman invites us to stop worrying about public debt, even urges us to love it / Opinion, The New York Times, Dec, 3. 2020/. Joining Oliver Blanchard, he sees a shift in fiscal paradigm, arguing that public debt is not a major problem Maybe for America, but definitely not for others, especially not for emerging economies. Having low interest rates due to lower inflation, that is the catch, the burden of debt is not what it used to be. It is realty funny that Krugman takes the Greek tragedy to support his argument. Due to huge public debts Greece fell from 85% of the EU average GDP level to 66% in the last decade, due to the financial crisis in 2010. The same can happen to some Club Med Euro area members in the next financial crisis. Can anyone rule out a major financial crisis in the 2020s? In the lack of the US dollar as the national currency, you must watch both, the level of public debt and the level of debt-servicing. Re Learn to stop worrying and love public debt Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Dolphins and whales
text: DOLPHINS AND WHALES Kiemelt temak John Thornhill is definitely right that the best venture capitalists have performed a vital capitalistic function by turning seemingly outlandish ideas and transformative technologies into everyday realities /FT, 4 February 2020/. They became reality in America, but they foiled to show up in Europe. Nevertheless, we have dolphins from Spotify to Technogym and many more. They will not be 1 trillion worth of new whales, but they can be even smarter, quicker and more flexible than their bigger, stronger and wealthier counterparts in America. They can appear in the emerging new economies of the EU by confining the competitive spirit of our workforce with new funds opened during the present crisis management. Re Venture capitalists should harpoon more whales Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Dragonflies are common, not dragons
text: DRAGONFLIES ARE COMMON, NOT DRAGONS Kicmelt temak It is perfectly right to say that the longer-term outlook for inflation remains to be clouded by the same secular, powerful forces that have kept it contained for decades. /Robin Wigglcsworth, FT, 27 March 2021/ Post-lockdown spending and base effects might increase inflation for a couple of quarters. However, inflation dynamics will not change, because they realty do not change on a dime /Jay Powell/. Even wage growth, which used to be the real leading indicator of broad-based inflation, ended its career in a softening Philips curve. In a post- and pre-pandemic world, inflation will be subdued exactly because the present pandemic has accelerated digital transition. New waves of the information revolution will result in decreasing prices across the board in the world economy. Dragonflies are much more common than dragons and fortunately, they are much less fierce. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Inflation bogeyman unsettles markets

Title: Economic thinking will stop Bidens experiment
text: ECONOMIC THINKING WILL STOP BIDENS EXPERIMENT Kicmelt temak American rescue plans might change the framework we use to understand policy /Megan Greene, FT, 5/7/2021/ but core economic thinking will halt newly reframed policy In the post-pandemic world, responsible fiscal policies will return In all previous chapters of all the crises in economic histoiy they did so. It was rationale in all cases, otherwise a new fiscal crisis would have occurred resulting in an across the board crisis in the economy. The Spanish Empire went bankrupt several times for not following this rule and finally the Bourbons took over from the Habsburgs. This side-effect might happen to America if they do not take into account prudent macroeconomic thinking. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Joe Bidens experiment could revolutionise economic thinking

Title: EUs unfinished business with the single market
text: EUS UNFINISHED BUSINESS WITH THE SINGLE MARKET Kicmelt temak In the beginning, both the EU and the UK will sutler huge losses due to Brexit. It is not a lose-win situation, the UKs losses are not the EUs wins. Blatantly, it is still not a win-win situation either. However, it could be. As Miriam Gonzalez Durantez rightly put it /FT, 13 Januaiy 2020/ both can win by responding to the shock of Brexit with new waves of regulatoiy reforms targeting stronger competitiveness and higher growth It is true that only Denmark scores better than the UK on the ease of doing business. It is also telling, that in the EU, there are still 83 types of trade obstacles to be abolished and 40 legislative measures to take in order to complete the single market. Instead of having a future catalogue of disasters coming from retaliations from both sides, we can capitalise on the strong catalyst coming from this divorce. Both, the EU and the UK need to be reformed to become strategic partners again Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re 'The EU must act to profit from the UKs Brexit losses"

Title: Europe enters permanent crisis mode
text: EUROPE ENTERS PERMANENT CRISIS MODE Kicmelt temak The feet of the matter is that the 19-member Eurozone was already on the brink of recession before the pandemic struck. /FT Big Read, 18 November 2020/ There were multiple crises by the outbreak of Covid-19. The EU had a permanent political crisis from 2015, an ongoing economic crisis from 2008, a Western identity crisis after 2016 and a family tragedy leading to the final divorce with the U.K. Then the pandemic hit and a complete health crisis was added to all the former problems. Europe was badly hit by the health crisis because they foiled to handle their previous crisis. In the lack of the ECBs funds and programs the EU might have had a complete disaster like in the last centuiys two world wars. Now, Europe needs efficient governments to abandon the permanent crisis mode we are in. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Eurozone economy: the struggle to stay afloat until a vaccine arrives

Title: Europe needs to climb the ladder
text: EUROPE NEEDS TO CLIMB THE LADDER Kicmelt temak All sincere and sober voices are more than welcomed with regard to the US. initiated America-China tensions - John Plender did his best by sending out the right noises. /Market Insights, FT, 3 Novenber 2020/ He is right that the Chinese government bond market, the second largest in the world, offers positive real interest income after allowing for inflation It means that developed countries pension funds can benefit from real incomes and they are able to pay retirement obligations. This is also true for all western institutional investors as well By now it is clear, that who decides to hurt China also hurts itself Indeed, by bashing Beijing the U.S. suffered more than China. That is the new power law in our global hut. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Chinese economy outstrips US despite Beijing bashing

Title: Europes rare moment of rational thinking
text: EUROPES RARE MOMENT OF RAHONAL THINKING Kicmelt temak The EU was absolutely right in signing an investment treaty between the EU and China. It did not hand China a strategic win /Gideon Rachman, FT, 5 Januaiy/, it followed the win-win strategy of all winners. We, Europeans, need to avoid a new cold war between the U.S. and China at nearly all costs. The new investment treaty supports that by opening up new business opportunities between Europe and China, between the West and the East. Business can benefit from both war and peace. Investments tend to capitalise on wealth creation in peaceful times, so they prefer peace to war. Good, that is the rationale of the exercise. According to game theoiy, it is always better to start the game as a dove and change just after the other becomes a predator. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Europe has handed China a strategic victory

Title: Europe should catch up with Asia in the CBDC endeavor
text: EUROPE SHOULD CATCH UP WITH ASIA IN THE CBDC ENDEAVOR Kicmelt temak The Bank of Korea is the latest central bank in the region to test a digital currency, following the path of the PBOC and the BoJ. They will examine the functionality of central bank digital currency in a virtual environment in order to introduce a digital won for broader use. The PBOC has been conducting public trials of its digital yuan in several cities for 8 months. In Europe both virtual and public trials of digital currencies are worth to launch In the meantime, all western and eastern experiments should be evaluated for the euro zone and also for other EU countries with their national currencies. This time it is a must for Europe not to be lagging behind America and Asia. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Bank of Korea to start CBDC trial in August

Title: Even America cannot run supersized deficits for ever
text: EVEN AMERICA CANNOT RUN SUPERSIZED DEFICITS FOR EVER Kicmelt temak Todays buzzword is debt sustainability/Free exchange, The Economist, June 5 th 2021/. Theoretically, fiscal free lunch is possible. When the interest rate on public debt is below the economys growth rate, existing debt burdens have no fiscal cost. America can run a deficit of 2.1 of GDP for ever so long as its debt is below 130% of GDP. However, it cannot do so forever. This option is only open for America. All other players have many unequal things, meaning that there is no such thing as a free lunch for the rest of the world. The present high European deficits and high public debt figures are not sustainable, especially not for the still vulnerable emerging economies outside the euro area. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Pace your debt

Title: Events, events and events
text: EVENTS, EVENTS AND EVENTS Kicmelt temak We all know the British Prime Ministers answer to the intimate question/what are you afraid of PM/: Events, events and events, my dear friend. Many sense the end of the party, spotting bubbles that finally will have to burst. Nevertheless, a trigger is always needed. It might be the rises in long-term interest rates. /Ruchir Sharma, FT, 1 march 2021/ It might be a new wave of the pandemic. It might be the opposite, a post-pandemic buying spree resulting in lower savings. It might also be the bond market pricing in higher inflation. Fifty years ago the German and the French government rejected Nixons call to buy US government bonds. Follow the money and geopolitics might have the upper hand to create the next trigger. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Export optimism must revive
text: EXPORT OPTIMISM MUST REVIVE Kicmelt temak Indeed, western economists tend to send out new marching orders, meaning that emerging countries should give up their successful export-led model of growth. /Arvind Subramanian, FT, 16 October 2020/ However, David Ricardo is all but dead and globalization is not a dead-end. Also, emerging countrys enterprises should strike the right balance between their global, regional and local markets. They must not give up any of them, just on the contrary, they should use all of them wisely. It means that in expanding overseas markets, where size matters more than ever, they have to find niches. In a nutshell, they have to find shrinking future niches where they can grow fest. In regional markets, they can find their own voices with a bigger share in one larger economic field. Locally, they can build up a holding structure with several branches covering at least two areas, where they test their talent, resources and potential to go regional and global Emerging countries can and should grow rapidly by gaining a larger share in all the three markets. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central bank of Hungary Re-Developing economies must not succumb to export pessimism

Title: Farming will be a family issue again
text: FARMING WILL BE A FAMILY ISSUE AGAIN Kicmelt temak We realty badly need a new farming revolution where food safety, quality control and the fight against obesity are at the very heart of a new model for forming /Donna Kilpatrick, FT, 31 July 2020/. It means, by definition, that we have to move away from industrial, destructive, monoculture forms of the present day forming, as our author put it rightly We should know our suppliers, direct-to-consumer sales will end in fomity-like ties between formers and consumers. We also need new ownership structures for forming to get rid of unhealthy and unsustainable big land-owners: the small will be beautiful again Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re A forming revolution is what we need in the crisis

Title: Fragility is the essence of life
text: 2021 FRAGILITY IS THE ESSENCE OF LIFE Kicmelt temak It is absolutely untrue, that we can diminish the fragility of the world economy by stopping aggressive monetaiy policies and huge accumulation of private debt. /Martin Wolf FT, 17 March 2021/ The world economy has become a huge and unified living organization through the permanent revolution of information technology that started in the 1970s. The present pandemic proved Natures Law once more: The more developed, the more fragile. Instead, we should reshape economic growth in order to improve the sustainability level of the world economy. We need smart, new, fair and globally available sustainable technologies in order to create a long-term sustainable economy and human mankind. We need more green and sustainable investment on both sides, governments and private businesses, meaning that we need more fiscal stimulus, monetaiy easing and private debts. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re  Economies can survive a stock market crash

Title: France is the biggest winner of Brexit
text: FRANCE IS THE BIGGEST WINNER OF BREXIT Kicmelt temak Some argue that Britains presence in the EU provided an element of balance /Philp Stephens, FT, 8 November 2019/ and due to Brexit, France would be a loser. Absolutely not, just on the contraiy. Britain used to be one of the biggest winners of the EU. Having lost its industrial base gained large export markets for the British service sector and via the opt-out policies it did not sutler from the euro and the austerity policies of the EU. It was blatant that Britain could not balance German power within the EU. France had close to zero negotiating power against German interests, with or without British support. Apart from America, France will be the biggest winner of Brexit. It will lose nothing and all southern members will join France to balance German power. Re France is a big loser from Brexit Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Germany's choice is Europe's future
text: GERMANYS CHOICE IS EUROPES FUTURE Kicmelt temak There is a clear-cut gap between Germanys EU policies and its national interests in the German-Russian relations. On one hand, the Germans seem to support the "professed ambition" /Tony Barber, FT, 16 Februaiy 2021/ of a United States of Europe via a coherent foreign and security policy for a mature power. On the other hand, they tiy to maintain their special relationship with Russia based on mutual interests in trade and investments. There is nothing to do with moral debt, the naked truth is business. Germany can either follow its economic interests as a member of the present European integration or must give them up, partly or entirety, in a much more binding United States of Europe. Besides, all Central and Eastern Europeans face the same dilemma and the V4 region has a ciystal-clear answer to that. We do not wish to be a part of a new empire, European or not, it does not realty matter. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Germanys bridges to Russia split open Europe

Title: Global recessions are not out-of-blue events any more
text: GLOBAL RECESSIONS ARE NOT OUT-OF-BLUE EVENTS ANY MORE Kicmelt temak Columnist Free exchange of The Economist claims that recessions can indeed appear as if out of the blue /The Economist, August 24th 2019/. Not anymore, in my view. As for the last global financial crisis, the collapse of Lehmann Brothers triggered all the events leading to the fully- fledged American and European crisis. Nevertheless, we had a long period between August 2007 and September 2008 when anything could happen and the due course of the next crisis was expected in 2010, not two years before. Timing might have been decided by the outgoing American administration not by market forces. Re A crisis of faith Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Globalists have already lost at home
text: GLOBALISTS HAVE ALREADY LOST AT HOME Kicmelt temak Janan Ganesh is of course right saying that Biden is the last, best hope for globalists /FT, 16 April/. There is only one snag. They have already lost at home, in America. The American strategy of using globalization to keep the 21 st centuiy for the US and allies worked well for decades. But, by the middle of the 2010s, an old/new thinking finally won foe argument. According to it, globalization helped China to rise more than America to keep global leadership, so the rules of game need to be changed. The complete American political elite seems to share this view by now. The new strategy is a mixture of less globalization and more regionalism Globalization as we know it now is over and new regional structures will emerge in the 2020s. Re Biden is the last, best hope for globalists Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

URL: Matolcsy: Central banks should be included to win the climate war
Title: Matolcsy: Central banks should be included to win the climate war
text: Matolcsy: Central banks should be included to win the climate war Mark Carney is absolutely right that we need to rewire our entire economies to mobilize 100 trillion dollars to win the war against climate change /FT, 30 October 2021/. It is most likely that the total amount of external finance needed for the sustainable energy drive over the next decades will be much bigger. All in all, we need all central banks to step in the ring. Central banks will create money, they will launch targeted QEs for buying green assets and central banks/regulators can restructure the decisions of the banking sector in the direction of green transition. Anyway, central banks were established to finance wars and/or help economies getting out of the ruins of wars and crisis. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re The world of finance will be judged on the lOOtn dollars climate challenge Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

URL: Matolcsy: We all need to be fair, just and efficient
Title: Matolcsy: We all need to be fair, just and efficient
text: Matolcsy: We all need to be fair, just and efficient The list of core global public goods seems to me much longer than Martin Wolf has put it recently /FT, 3 November 2021/. Beyond prosperity, peace and protection of our planet we also need mutual fairness, justice without double standards, the recognition of the right of all nations to rise, free access to global trade and many more. When someone labels China as an example of centralized despotism and misunderstands the US calling it a crumbling democracy, it does not help. It hurts the global public goods of fairness, justice and the right of a nation to prosper. It might give the unhealthy moral basis for future adventures trying to get rid of a country from the access to global trade. In the US the Founding Fathers aimed for a Republic, not a democracy and they really received what they dreamt of. China is a well- governed centralized state that works efficiently to give prosperity to all citizens. In both cases labelling is not fair, not just and will not be an efficient tool to save our global public goods. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re How we can share our divided world Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

URL: Matolcsy: The 50ys American parallel went global
Title: Matolcsy: The 50ys American parallel went global
text: Matolcsy: The 50ys American parallel went global Edward Luce is absolutely right seeing todays parallels with the US of the 1970s /FT, 14 January 2022/. The 1970s really had the meme of rising inflation, spiralling crime, political drift and ominous geopolitics in America. The 1970s was really a transitional decade between the 1930s and the 1980s. However, in the 1970s we had the same patterns worldwide due to the triggers of 1968 /Prague and Paris/, 1971 and the two oil crisis. Fifty years later we start to recognize the same patterns globally due to the former American strategic decisions on the pandemic, the US- China relationship and Russia. However, all the engines of change in the 2020s are bigger, stronger, faster and much more complex than they were in the 1970s. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Americas nagging echoes of the 1970s Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

URL: Matolcsy: The three major trends of 2022
Title: Matolcsy: The three major trends of 2022
text: Matolcsy: The three major trends of 2022 Ruchir Sharma offers ten economic trends that could define 2022 /FT, 4 January 2022/. Some seem to be relevant, some are not so convincing. May I offer three other trends that might have a bigger impact on 2022 than Sharmas. Firstly, there is still the new wave/s/ of the pandemic leading to a hybrid year: the first half is still determined by the virus, the second half could be better. Secondly, the new waves of inflation and the monetary policy changes of central banks will have a huge impact on the global economy. Thirdly, we start to recognize the return, rerun and parallels of two former decades of the last century: the 1970s and the 1940s. It means that governments, central banks and business sectors will start to reshape their mindsets about their political and business strategies. Big states, big central banks and big global geopolitical games will be with us for the whole 2020s. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Ten economic trends that could define 2022 Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

URL: Matolcsy: Top 10 major trends of Europe in the last 20ys
Title: Matolcsy: Top 10 major trends of Europe in the last 20ys
text: Matolcsy: Top 10 major trends of Europe in the last 20ys For global financial investors, the Top 10 significant trends of the last 20ys were really that Gary Greenberg has identified recently /P WMNET.com/. As for Europe, the picture seems to be a little bit different from the global picture. Rise of China, tehnology as a driving force, end of myth of US as a partner and decline of commodity countries are among them, but some others played an even bigger role in Europes last two decades. The introduction of the euro can be regarded as the single most significant step. It helped German to fly and resulted in the fall of the Club- Med countries. Ten European countries joined the EU in the first decade and some of them /especially Poland and Hungary/ tend to be the new forces to reform the Union. The migration crisis in 2015 reshaped European politics, since then the debate on migration, defending the EUs borders, reforming EUs policies has been deepening the division between Western and Eastern members of the EU. Germany became too strong in Europe and too weak in global politics. By the beginning of the 2020s the EU seems to be on the right track to a German Europe instead of a European Germany. The European Central Bank has been showing a successful evolution path from a lame duck between 2008 and 2012 to the present efficient crisis management of Covid-19. Finally, the new/old division between Europe and Russia reemerged as the unpleasant side effect of the new American strategy. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Top 10 significant trends of the last 20 years. Gary Greenberg. URL: Matolcsy: Fears of durable inflation are justified
Title: Matolcsy: Fears of durable inflation are justified
text: Matolcsy: Fears of durable inflation are justified Some central banks and financial experts regard the return of durable inflation as wildly premature /Robin Wigglesworth, FT Markets Insight 2 November 2020/. Am afraid the opposite is true. It is absolutely right to assume that we entered a new era for monetary policy due to the rerun of the 1970ys /and quite frankly the 1940s/. Both, the decade 50 years ago and the 2020s were ignited by the American Grand Strategy to keep the leading position of the incumbent western world power, the American Empire. At that time and in the beginning of our decade American decisions started a chain-reaction in the global economy that resulted in durable inflation, the accumulation of huge public debts, political and social unrest in nearly all western countries and many more unpleasant side- effects. America could not stop the chain-reaction until Paul Volcker put an end to it. It is still too early to say that globalization, technology, demographics, debt burdens and the weakening bargaining power of labour all remain the same as they were in the last 40ys. Nothing will remain the same when a new global chain-reaction is in play. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re The dawn of the quantitative tightening era? Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

URL: Matolcsy: What large central banks can learn from smaller ones
Title: Matolcsy: What large central banks can learn from smaller ones
text: Matolcsy: What large central banks can learn from smaller ones I could not agree more with Nannette Hechler-Faydherbe that large economies can learn from smaller ones /FT, Opinion Market Insights, 2022/. Indeed, Switzerland sticks out as the best European teacher, globally Dubai, and the UAE, are the outstanding examples. However, larger central banks can also learn from smaller ones. Within the EU, the National Bank of Hungary sent out the first signals that inflation threat was imminent. After the first warnings MNB went further confirming that there would not only be spikes of inflation but also a long period of higher inflation would come as well. MNB was the first central bank in the EU launching the complete overhaul of monetary policy by increasing the base-rate, also saying that it would not be a one-off step, a long cycle would come. MNB has been following a flexible monetary policy that enables the central bank to raise different rates monthly and weekly. Other central banks in the region were also among the early birds in changing their monetary regimes. The main lesson to be learnt from smaller central banks is that new inflation-related forward guidance should go hand in hand with changes in the monetary policy regime of a central bank. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re What large economies can learn from smaller ones____________________________________________________________________________ Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

URL: Matolcsy: Reducing public debt by unleashing growth potential
Title: Matolcsy: Reducing public debt by unleashing growth potential
text: Matolcsy: Reducing public debt by unleashing growth potential The EU indeed is in the trap of interacting vulnerabilities /Barbara Baarsma, Roel Beetsma, VOX EU 18 January 2022/. Presently, the limited growth potential makes it difficult to reduce high /on average, 100% of GDP in the euro area/ public debt. Also, accumulated vulnerabilities - high private and public debts, declining growth potential, faltering convergence among EU members, high unemployment rates in the Club-Med countries, outdated tax systems, rigid labor force regulations, lack of leading global companies, etc. - tend to create vicious circles. All of these threaten political stability. Limit resilience of the business sector and undermine solidarity in the EU. A New Growth Plan is badly needed to come out of this trap because the only viable path for reducing private and public debt ratios is to unleash the growth potential of all EU member states. It might sound unfair, but reducing debts will be a punishment unless we have the gifts of extra economic growth. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re: Reducing public debt need not be a punishment Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

URL: Matolcsy: Chinas economy enters the new world of the 2020s
Title: Matolcsy: Chinas economy enters the new world of the 2020s
text: Matolcsy: Chinas economy enters the new world of the 2020s The Economist fails to recognize the gist of economic policy changes in China. They focus on lockdowns and crackdowns, instead of the accelerated transition of the Chinese economy from a former successful growth model to the new growth path of the 2020s /The Economist, Jan 22nd 2022/. China rightly spotted the very nature of the new decade. These are warring times, the previous peaceful global economic order is over. There are new types of hostilities from pandemics to sanctions, there is war-time inflation and new energy shocks fueled by geopolitical decisions. In a nutshell, we entered the chapter of a new cold war initiated by the American Empire. China rightly expects new waves of surprises in the global financial system and in international trade. All these unpleasant changes will accelerate Chinas transition to a new growth path based on sustainable energy sources, new technologies, high-end products and services, smart government/central banks regulations, central banks digital currency, and many more. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re As Chinas economy slows, policymakers seek to revive growth____________________________________________________________________ Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

URL: Matolcsy: Time has come to ban crypto trading and mining in the EU
Title: Matolcsy: Time has come to ban crypto trading and mining in the EU
text: Matolcsy: Time has come to ban crypto trading and mining in the EU China declared all cryptocurrency activities illegal last September and Russias central bank proposes ban on crypto trading and mining /Max Seddon and Eva Szalay, Jan 20 2022, FT/. I perfectly agree with the proposal and also support the senior EU financial regulators point that the EU should ban the mining method used to produce most new bitcoin. It is clear-cut that cryptocurrencies could service illegal activities and tend to build up financial pyramids. Russias central bank is right saying that the breakneck growth and market value of cryptocurrencies is defined primarily by speculative demand for future growth, which creates bubbles. The EU should act together in order to preempt the building up of new financial pyramids and financial bubbles. EU citizens and companies would be allowed to own cryptocurrencies abroad and regulators will track their holdings. URL: Matolcsy: Ending a period of financial nonsense
Title: Matolcsy: Ending a period of financial nonsense
text: Matolcsy: Ending a period of financial nonsense Borrowing costs for southern Eurozone governments jumped close to pre-pandemic hights due to the somewhat hawkish shift of ECBs communication on raising interest rates soon /FT, Eurozone economy, Martin Arnold, February 7 2022/. Indeed, Eurozone inflation would stay at 4 per cent for most of this year, so the unanimous concern of the ECBs governing council is more than justified. This is also a signal that the period of negative rates for heavily indebted southern Eurozone economies is coming to an end. It was really a piece of financial nonsense that Greek bond yields turned negative last year. Persistently high inflation might have a positive impact on European financial decisions by forcing governments and central banks to end the policy of negative interest rates. URL: Matolcsy: Time is a scarce resource for central banks
Title: Matolcsy: Time is a scarce resource for central banks
text: Matolcsy: Time is a scarce resource for central banks Indeed, it took way too long for the Fed and ECB to correct their misread of price increases and they risk a pile-up of monetary policy tightening as inflation expectations become more embedded /Mohamed El-Erian, FT, February 6 2022/. Both leading central banks try to regain their policy credibility after their mistakes maintaining their call about the transitory nature of inflation for far too long. They should have opted for a smooth transition for monetary policy and the economy instead of a continued misreading of inflation figures. When it comes to the ECB, they will not be able to maintain both, negative interest rates and their huge influence over eurozone bond markets. They have to choose between a smooth path heading for positive rates or buying up the 100 percent of debt, as they did in the last two years. Time is a scarce resource for even giant central banks, so they have to accelerate their decision making process. They lost the inflation- narrative but they still win the war against future anticipated inflation. URL: Matolcsy: The decade of rare success stories is coming
Title: Matolcsy: The decade of rare success stories is coming
text: Matolcsy: The decade of rare success stories is coming Yes, the post-pandemic world shaped by depopulation, declining productivity, deglobalisation and debt, the four Ds, is likely result in even slower growth and higher inflation /Ruchir Sharma, FT 14 February 2022/. Against the backdrop of the four Ds, global productivity growth might fall back below 1%, interest rates head higher, labor force continues to shrink and wages are rising. The result is persistently high inflation. Growth in high-income countries might really slow down below 2%, in fast-growing larger emerging economies below 5%, between the two many smaller emerging economies will be happy with a GDP growth figure between 3-4% for the 2020s. There might be rare exceptions to these figures. Those will belong to the club who successfully swim against the tide of the four Ds world by defeating inflation, focusing on productivity gains and solving the bottle-necks of shrinking labor force. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Slower growth and higher inflation are the hallmarks of a post-Covid world Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

URL: Matolcsy: Targeted means will be coming soon
Title: Matolcsy: Targeted means will be coming soon
text: Matolcsy: Targeted means will be coming soon Indeed, markets could not rely on the predictable and abundant liquidity provided by central banks in the new era of higher inflation /Mohamed El-Erian, FT, Markets Insights 22 February 2022/. Financial markets are losing the anchor of central banks QE programs and low interest rates that created abundant and predictable liquidity for the whole business sector worldwide. Due to higher inflation, central banks will be forced to withdraw nearly all the major elements of their previous monetary policies. Nevertheless, we can find an old/new anchor to provide abundant liquidity in niches for the banking sector. These might be the targeted CBs programs similar to the former Funding for Lending Scheme of the BoE and the Funding for Growth Scheme of the National Bank of Hungary. PBOC is also running a well-crafted targeted program for the SME sector. Instead of universal abundance and all-time predictable liquidity, we should aim for market niches, like sustainability, by using new targeted CBs programs. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re There is more to market volatility than Ukraine Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

URL: Matolcsy: CBDCs will come as game changers
Title: Matolcsy: CBDCs will come as game changers
text: Matolcsy: CBDCs will come as game changers Project Hamilton, the collaboration of the MIT and the Boston Fed, successfully completed the first phase of their joint central bank digital currency /CBDC/ infrastructure project in February /Riley Steward, FT, Central Banking, 08 Feb 2022/. They were able to process 100 000 transactions per second, meaning that a CBDC system could process the normal economic volume of transactions. In addition to that, a good part of the transactions appeared to scale as researchers added more servers. We can start to think about a new Moore-Law, calling it the Hamilton-law, as happened in the course of the evolution of chips. After Poject Hamilton releases the privacy and user-interface /UI/ components of the design phase two will be complete. If they get both right, all of us - costumers, business sectors, banks, central banks and governments- will be firmly convinced by the advantages of CBDC. It is because people will not be losing money to fraudsters like they do with cryptocurrencies, as Professor Bohme was cited in the MIT-Fed project. As soon as we can cut out one of the main risks of crypto-currencies while keeping all the other wins, we will gain a new game changer in the financial world.
