URL: Matolcsy: We are not prepared for the dramas of the 2020s
Title: Matolcsy: We are not prepared for the dramas of the 2020s
text: Matolcsy: We are not prepared for the dramas of the 2020s According to Martin Rees /FT, Opinion, 22 February 2022/catastrophes can happen slowly /like climate change/ or rarely /like pandemics/. Nevertheless, both can happen quickly and regularly as well. Just a couple of days after publishing his article we witnessed the outbreak of the Russian-Ukrainian war, the new and new waves of western sanctions, the explosion of commodity prices and many more out-of-the blue events. As the inquiry of the House of Lords put it rightly: The pandemic has exposed the UKs risk management system as deficient and too inflexible to provide the protection our nation needs. We should expect sudden dramas unfolding in the 2020s due to the nature of chain-reactions and also because the 2020s tend to repeat some major patterns of the 1940s and the 1970s. Both decades proved to be full of risks of unexpected and really unpleasant events. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary After Covid. Britain must learn to plan properly for extreme risk_____________________________________________________________ Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

URL: Matolcsy: New hypes might use some retro policies
Title: Matolcsy: New hypes might use some retro policies
text: Matolcsy: New hypes might use some retro policies Aveek Bhattacharya is perfectly right coming up with the issue of future public sector reforms where retro policies of the past might be of some worth /FT, Opinion, 18 February 2022/. In our decade the risk of stagflation, falling productivity, new black and green swans, new wars and many more will trigger public sector reforms in order to counterbalance the damages caused by the old/new patterns of the 2020s. There are really three avenues for future reforms. Firstly, we should ensure that service delivery is evidence-based, readopting the mantra what works. Secondly, we can bet big on new technologies, like innovations in robotics, Al, nanotechnology and communications. Thirdly, public services should be more human and individualized. All the three paths should be followed at the same time. For reforming our public sectors, however, we need the same standards for all the three solutions. We must measure everything, we need mandatory evaluations and we have to initiate widespread knowledge-sharing. Public sector reforms might be able to help private sectors to survive the dramas of the 2020s. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re  The future case for a retro policy: public sector reform____________________________________________________________________ Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

URL: Matolcsy: Central banks should be given a CBDC mandate
Title: Matolcsy: Central banks should be given a CBDC mandate
text: Matolcsy: Central banks should be given a CBDC mandate Presently, the majority of global central banks lack the legal authority to issue CBDC /Central banking staff, Central Banking, 2/15/2022/. In my view, all central banks should be given the full authority to issue their digital currencies in order to provide the whole financial system with a regulated path to the transition from the present petrodollar/Eurodollar system to a new one. CBDCs can mix credit, fiscal easing, Al, Big Data, block chain technologies and even cryptocurrencies in order to help the global financial system creating the new, geopolitically divided - western and eastern - world of global finance. CBDCs will also let us to use targeted means instead of general QEs. In the lack of CBDCs we will not be able to follow the orderly closure of the outgoing global financial order prevailed between 1996 and 2021. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Majority of central banks lack the legal authority to issue CBDC_________________________________________________________________ Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

URL: Matolcsy: Environmental risks are much larger than climate risks
Title: Matolcsy: Environmental risks are much larger than climate risks
text: Matolcsy: Environmental risks are much larger than climate risks Indeed, climate risks can directly affect monetary policies and financial stability /Central banking staff, Central Banking 1/12/2022/. However, there are even bigger environmental risks coming from the sea-change in the geopolitical decisions of the global powers. When it comes to energy, finance, food, raw materials, rare earth metals, access to global transport and soon water supplies, it is still not climate change, but the total U-turn of global politics that play the major role in all these calamities. We might rerun the global crisis of the Seventeenth Century /as it was shown so brilliantly by Professor Geoffrey Parker/, when after the year of 1638, environmental catastrophes led to the explosion of prices and shortages globally, resulting in worldwide revolts, revolutions and major political changes. Nearly 400 years later major geopolitical changes seem to lead to very similar results and environmental green-swans can even strengthen and accelerate all these trends. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Few central banks cover environmental risk Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

URL: Matolcsy: Wikipedia needs a complete overhaul
Title: Matolcsy: Wikipedia needs a complete overhaul
text: Matolcsy: Wikipedia needs a complete overhaul It is certainly fair to say that we should not expect Wikipedia to be the final arbiter of truth /John Thornhill, FT, Opinion 18 March 2022/. It has indeed its flaws, biases and blind spots meaning that it is not 100% reliable. Nevertheless, it should be because it belongs to the group of public goods. It is most likely one of the last best places on the Internet, however, as Taha Yasseri also says: It is a very good place to start your research but a terrible place to end your research. Period. It has frequently been used by trolls and many more biased players. It can be really very hard to remove even blatant errors in reports from allegedly reliable sources. When it comes to human beings /they might even be politicians, bankers, central bankers/ these imperfections tend to be really embarrassing and misleading. Concerning personalities, both living and who passed away, we or our families should be given the chance to correct the artificially flawed character of our personalities pictured in Wikipedia, including the removal of all the pieces proved to be evidently wrong. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re The truth about war is messy - just read Wikipedia________________________________________________________________________________ Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

URL: Matolcsy: The future of money and the money of the future
Title: Matolcsy: The future of money and the money of the future
text: Matolcsy: The future of money and the money of the future Eswar Prasad new book on the future of money covers all the plans, dreams and fears of central bankers. We have been facing a couple of really hunting dilemmas since 1996. The disruption of the traditional ways of creating money was really kick started by the launching of the Internet. Our dilemmas were even sharpened and deepened since 2021, when a new global financial system /actually two, a western and an eastern one/ started to emerge. Out of the main dilemmas of course the future of CBDCs is at the very heart of all our thinking. We all - central bankers, bankers, law makers, governments, fintech companies, cryptocurrency players and costumers - seek for the right mixture of decentralization of making money and the security of the privately managed payment systems. This is exactly what CBDCs can offer through building up a backstop to all privately managed transactions. Having launched CBDCs we can further strengthen financial inclusion, we can improve monetary policy transmission, we can secure cross-border payments and we can even fight tax-evasion or corruption. We do not need to bypass banks, just on the contrary, this would be a 3.0 financial system of central banks, traditional banks/financial institutions and all the members of the new disruptive financial world. All in all, the money of the future coincides with the future of money. The outcome will be the fusion of freedom and security in our financial systems. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Eswar Prasad, The Future of Money: How the Digital Revolution is Transforming Currencies and Finance Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

Title: Matolcsy: Targeted fiscal and monetary policies are needed
text: Matolcsy: Targeted fiscal and monetary policies are needed Western policy makers have been watching the Fed in order to gain some insights about the normalization of financial conditions in the near future /Raghuram G. Rajan, Project Syndicate Jan.31, 2022 /. The Federal Reserve will either prolong the party or will tighten its monetary policy significantly to control inflation. So there might be either the rerun of the Fed normalization policies in 1982 or the Fed answers to the irrational exuberance of 1996 by doing nothing. In my view, however, it is not to normalize or not is the key to the future. For both, fiscal and monetary policies the vital question is how to use targeted spending and central banks programs in order to strengthen inclusive economic growth, creating more jobs and fasten the transition to a sustainable path. Neither normal nor the present more than unorthodox fiscal and monetary policies cannot do the job because in this unusually turbulent decade everything is getting more and more non-linear. In this new Quantum-world linear, predictable, normal or not universal policies are not working anymore. We need targeted watering in the Negev desert called the global economy to survive our decade. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re The End of Free Lunch Economics Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

Title: Matolcsy: The era of still-cheap-money is coming
text: Matolcsy: The era of still-cheap-money is coming It is certainly true that the era of super-cheap money is ending /The Economist, Feb 1 st 2022/. The world economy has been really heavily indebted, where the stock of global debt has gone from 83 trillion dollars in 2000 to around 295 trillion dollars in 2021. This rate was nearly double the pace of world GDP growth. Debt rose from 230% of GDP in 2000 to 320% on the eve of the pandemic. Due to the pandemic it has gone to 355% last year. Yes, central banks have to battle the surge of inflation resulting in much higher interest rates globally. The total global costs of interests were 11% of GDP in 2021 and they might go up to 15% of projected GDP by 2026. In a worse forecast the interest bill could rise to about 20 trillion dollars by 2026, nearly a fifth of GDP. On one hand, we are closing down the era of super-cheap money, on the other hand we are entering the era of still-cheap-money. Especially governments could afford the luxury to pay higher interest bills because they can borrow more cheaply than private-sector borrowers and they might foot the bill via higher taxes. They will definitely do, so the rate of piling up debts will be again double the rate of GDP growth globally. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re The global interest bill is about to jump Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

Title: Matolcsy: Wishful thinking will not help
text: Matolcsy: Wishful thinking will not help One of the best western financial expert made his bet on a weakening China-Russia alliance /Rushir Sharma, FT Opinion 28 March 2022/. It is wishful thinking in my view, they will come even closer due to the mounting pressures of the American Grand Strategy. When it comes to Chinese property markets it is really one of the best news that the focus of economic growth starts to change, weakening the link between GDP growth and the credit growth for property developments. As for demography, China will finally solve the looming fewer workers -slower growth trap by launching the new three children policies. Concerning the success story of Chinas state capitalism, all the historical breakthroughs have been coming by using both, the state and the private sector at the same time. The new flourishing private sector did not replace state-run companies to create a brand-new export sector, they were really new. It is not the retreat of the state, it is the ancient/modern concept of benefiting from both, private /yin/ and state /yang/ energies. Anyway, a G2 cooperation would be much better for both worlds than the unfolding G-2 world. Governing Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re China is less likely to back Russia while facing its own troubles Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

Title: Matolcsy: Writings on the wall
text: Matolcsy: Writings on the wall... It is high time to read the warnings of one of the best living historians. According to Harold James more connections -not less- will help prevent an Era of Scarcity /Foreign Affairs, February 2, 2022/. Does it really matter that we are heading towards a new autarchy or we open a new golden age of globalization? It depends on our vision for the future. If one seeks for the rerun of the 20th century, with three world wars, bloody revolutions, unprecedented human losses the likely answer is: who cares? If someone else would like to avoid the rerun of the Thirty Years War of the Seventeenth Century and the huge human sacrifices of the last century, the answer is crystal clear. It says: Let us rule out the new Era of Scarcity via opening the way for a new chapter of globalization. Out of all shortages, the deficiencies of human memories and the shortcomings of our historical knowledge tend to pose the single most dangerous threats to our future. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re The Supply Chain Crisis and the Future of Globalization Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

Title: Matolcsy: The Fifth Wave
text: Matolcsy: The Fifth Wave Peter Thiel, the extremely successful and creative libertarian tech investor challenged the old-school financial figures, accusing them of trying to lock cryptocurrencies out /Richard Waters, FT, Financials 9 April/10 April 2022/. In each 25 years a new global financial regime has been emerging since the beginning of the 1920s. The second wave started around 1946, after closing World War II, within the framework of the Bretton Woods Agreement. The third wave was launched 25ys later by the US president in 1971. The fourth wave was triggered by the beginning of the Internet in 1996. In a somewhat hidden way, the fifth wave has been unfolding since 2021. As in the beginning of the former one, it was still not clear-cut that we opened a new chapter in the modem history of finance. However, we have definitely begun our journey towards a new global financial regime last year. Within this fifth wave of modern global financial regimes we will witness the birth of many more cryptocurrencies, new CBDCs, a new divided G-2 world instead of a G2 cooperation between the US and China, a rebirth of the role for gold and new technologies in finance. All of them will fight all the others, similarly to the skirmishes between Peter Thiel and Warren Buffet. The same happened to the Protestant Churches and figures in Sixteen Century Europe after 1517. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re  Warren Buffett is bitcoins enemy number one, says PayPal founder Peter Thiel Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

Title: Matolcsy: We need two budgets in one
text: Matolcsy: We need two budgets in one The EU should rewrite its fiscal rules /Martin Sandbu, FT, Opinion 2/3/22/. Nevertheless, there are no one-fit-all solutions for all EU member countries. We can count on three building elements for the new fiscal regime that might last until the end of this seven years EU-budget. Firstly, the Rubicon of joint borrowing for cross-border transfers has been really crossed, meaning that the EU can borrow heavily in the coming years. Secondly, the EU badly needs an investment-intensive growth path, however, there are different avenues for the 27 member countries. The Northern Group of the EU needs to focus on the new high-tech industries instead of the present mid-technologies. The Southern Belt of the Eurozone needs something very different /sun, soil and the sweetness of life/, while the emerging EU economies need a fusion of Europes past successes /mainly huge infra projects/ and the future of the EU /new technologies/. Thirdly, France and Italy are right saying that some types of investment /like digital and green transition/ have the merit to be financed by the budget. All in all, we need two budgets in one, where the first traditional part should be under 3% of the GDP and the second part - mainly financed by joint borrowing- should be allowed to add an extra 3% to the first one. Governor Matolcsy, MNB the Central Bank of Hungary Re The EU should rewrite its fiscal rules Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

Title: Matolcsy: 1638  2022
text: Matolcsy: 1638-2022 Maybe the Governor of the Bank of England is right telling us that We are a very long way away from the 1970s. Maybe Karen Ward is right that the spectre of the 1970s turmoil haunts the UK economy /FT, Companies and Markets, 15 March 2022/. Maybe we are facing an even bigger challenge than the rerun of the 1970s /and also the 1940s/. Maybe we have something even bigger in play than the 50ys and 80ys cycles of history. When it comes to longer cycles, we should be pondering the rerun of the Seventeenth Century in our times, especially the present global rerun of Europes Thirty Years War between 1618 and 1648. The good news is that we started to handle the threats of the present climate change. The bad news is that we should also handle the impacts of the geopolitical climate change of our times that might result in the same scarcities, revolts and turmoil, what our ancestors faced globally in the Seventeenth Century. Then bad weather, now bad geopolitical decisions have devastating effects on our life. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Spectre of 1970s turmoil haunts the UK economy Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

Title: Matolcsy: It is permanent, not transitory
text: Matolcsy: It is permanent, not transitory It has been a debate about the nature of global inflation since 2021, coming from the Covid-related production disruptions in global value chains /Martin Sandbu, FT, Opinion 20 April 2022/. By now, more and more politicians and central bankers start to recognize the similar patterns between the 1970s and the 2020s, even between the 1940s and the 2020s. All the calamities started to show up in 2020 will continue, as the historical patterns are unfolding and getting stronger and stronger. It definitely means that credit, capital, labour, knowledge, information, data and all other essential resources must move from one sector to another. Indeed, the faster the better. Higher interest rates and tougher monetary policies will support this transitions because they push governments and central banks to launch joint targeted policies, credit lines and tax incentives for future winners. Central bankers should consider higher global inflation as permanent in our decade, so they must not ease off the brakes. In the meantime, they can initiate targeted programs hand in hand with their governments with preferential terms for green, digital and sustainable projects. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re  Central bankers should think twice before pressing the brake even harder Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

Title: Matolcsy: Towards the post-neoliberal era
text: Matolcsy: Towards the post-neoliberal era Indeed, the process of creating a new Bretton Woods Agreement has just begun /Rana Foroohar, FT, Opinion 18 April/. In a clear-cut speech at the Atlantic Council, the brilliant economist and US Treasury secretary relinked trade to values. According to the 80ys cycle we are still in 1942, meaning that in principle it is still too early to the recap of Churchills Fulton-speech - but this is exactly what happened. However, history does not repeat itself with the same events in the same row, instead patterns tend to be the same. In 1938 neoliberalism was invented, by 2018 the seeds of a new era called post-neoliberalism were in place. In 1943 the US approved a post-war strategy based on a paper of Oscar Morgenstern and John von Neumann and the Bretton Woods Agreement was born in 1944. All these events led to a divided world by 1948. Since the beginning of the 1990s a neoliberal era has been operating within the one world- two systems framework. This era is coming to an end and we will definitely end up with a new bipolar system. Eighty years ago the level of personal freedom seemed to be the dividing line between the two worlds, this time the level of personal and national security might be the main difference. The choice is ours. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re It is time for a new Bretton Woods Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

Title: Matolcsy: ECBs delay is due to the two-in-one Eurozone
text: Matolcsy: ECBs delay is due to the two-in-one Eurozone The ECB is definitely overdue about starting normalization of monetary policy. They might be concerned about financial market stability, where the key concern appears to be Italy /Moritz Kraemer, FT, Opinion Market Insights, April 25 2022/. However, the key to why the ECB does not follow the US Federal Reserve or the Bank of England is the built-in division of the structure of the Eurozone. The Northern and the Southern parts have totally different stakes in the new stagflation-type decade. In booming times all these differences can be handled smoothly, in stormy times there are no good options for both. ECB should not be afraid of following other global central banks in reshaping their monetary policies. In the meantime, they should also open new avenues for the Southern Belt via targeted credit lines in order to maintain GDP growth. Economic growth can better support financial stability than super-loose interest rates. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Italy can deal with higher interest rates Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

Title: Matolcsy: The economic side-effects of major political decisions
text: Matolcsy: The economic side-effects of major political decisions Present high inflation globally can be attributed to the US and other Western economies that have misgoverned internally while sowing discord and bullying externally. Chinas low inflation acts as a significant stabilizer for global prices /Global Times, Apr. 24/. In the beginning of the 1970s, the US Grand Strategy started a decade by some major political decisions aiming for reigning in Germany and Japan. All the decisions resulted in a tormented, high-inflation, low growth decade for the global economy. The US economy suffered huge losses, finally Paul Volker defeated inflation. The price-tag for America was even higher than the damage caused by the US decisions for the economic rivals. Since the outbreak of the pandemic we have been re-running the 1970s. In the 2020s the patterns seem to be similar to the 70s, meaning that economic side-effects will be much higher than anyone imagined of. Be careful what you dream of. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re US. other Western countries foment global high inflation: experts Copyright 2021, Magyar Nemzeti Bank

Title: Higher but not runaway inflation is coming
text: HIGHER BUT NOT RUNAWAY INFLAHON IS COMING Kiemelt temak We are just in the midst of a dilemma about the future of inflation Professor Jeremy Siegel is probably right in saying that inflation will run well above the Feds 2% target and will do so for several years; however, no hyperinflation can be seen on the horizon /FT, 20 January 2021/ Nevertheless, a couple of other factors might play their roles in the future of inflation First of all, we do not measure inflation property because we foil to include all the effects of the ongoing technological revolution, especially the impact of digital transition Nowadays, we might have much lower inflation than we see in our statistics. So, we might have some empty places to fill in The US will gradually replace China with other emerging Asian economies in its trade. That probably will have the same impact on prices in the US as during the rising periods of the US-China trade. Also, the digital transition in the American economy will definitely accelerate parity in response to the huge and efficient digital transformation of the Chinese economy. Besides, we have learnt a lot from the damages caused by the hyperinflation of the 1920s and the 1970s. At present, no one is realty interested in a runaway inflation globally and in the US. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Higher inflation is coming and it will hit bondholders

Title: History is full of unintended side-effects
text: HISTORY IS FULL OF UNINTENDED SIDE-EFFECTS Kicmelt temak Indeed, Russian fiscal and monetaiy policies have become a model of orthodoxy since 2015. /Ruchir Sharma, FT, 29 March 2021/ It was a wise and successful answer to all Western sanctions. The Russian model works, a crisis-scarred nation rightly prizes stability and policies aiming for import substitution which created a new SME sector. Russia is real!/ well-built to capitalize on a post-pandemic world where regionalism, local digital transition, Al, robotics and all other new technologies will play a major role in generating economic growth. It is clear-cut that all Western sanctions have been accelerating the transition from an Atlantic Age to the Age of Eurasia. Historically, all these were - most likely - an unintended side-effect of Western grand-strategies. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Fresh sanctions may barely dent Fortress Russia

Title: Hopefully more sophisticated warfare, not a war
text: HOPEFULLY MORE SOPHISHCATED WARFARE, NOT A WAR Kicmelt temak There is always a risk for war between the incunbent and the emerging new powers, but hopefully not this time. /John Dizard, FT, 30 Januaiy 2021/ When the stakes are too high for both of them, they must and will find other types of warfare to weaken the other side. Like in 1943, when Morgenstern and Neumann gave the mathematics of the future cold war to the Joint Force, the U.S. might opt for a new strategy. Technological, cyber and financial warfare will prevail over traditional war. This creates new risks for the global business sector, not less threatening than all the risks coming from outright warfare. Beyond that, it offers huge new business opportunities, as it happened to the financial community in the financial warfare during the 1970s and the 1980s. Governor, Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re The battle ahead: war is coming for your money'

Title: It is digital transformation in full speed
text: IT IS DIGITAL TRANSFORMAHON IN FULL SPEED Kicmelt temak Like in the 1940s, new technologies will change the world in the 2020s, this time, hopefully, for the better. Equity investors should cheer low rates indeed /Gillian Tett, FT, 17 September 2020/ because they are the somewhat hidden but strong driving force behind digital transformation Huge amounts of equity are needed to fuel all these changes. Equity trumps credit and governments are needed to join innovators by investing heavily to create a completely new social environment. Beyond this digital wave, there is the green transformation, starting to unfold, the revolution in demography is on its way, the sustainability thinking5 is gaining ground and a sweeping financial revolution is approaching. Anyway, technological revolutions bode much better for the future than full-blown wars. Re Equity investors should raise a glass to low rates Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: It is not only ethical, but strategic as well
text: IT IS NOT ONLY ETHICAL, BUT STRATEGIC AS WELL Kicmelt temak Martin Wolfis right saying that this pandemic is an ethical challenge /FT, Wednesday 25 March/. However, it is more than that, it is also a strategic challenge. It is not only a coincidence that they come together: in our interconnected global village big challenges are partly strategic and partly ethical. You cannot flourish, even survive by choosing unethical strategies. Surety, if the euro zone is not able to act together and northern countries do not show solidarity to the southern members, the European project will be morally and strategically dead. It is time to follow our best interest by showing solidarity to each other. Re This pandemic is an ethical challenge Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: It is not the EUs rescue fund that matters
text: IT IS NOT THE EUS RESCUE FUND THAT MATTERS Kicmelt temak It is certainty true that todays crisis is characterized by a simultaneous supply and demand shock /Wolfgang Munchau, FT, 27 April 2020/. But it is not the EUs late and inefficient response to the crisis that matters, it is the lack of a complete U-turn of economic policies that would keep the EU out in the dark in the 2020s. Behind the weak response we find all the earlier elements of misguided economic policies of the past decade. The lack of a complete overhaul of taxation in the member states, the missing giant EU-wide infrastructure projects, the absence of digital transformation, the shy-away attitude to reforming the Eurozone are all the real causes of the laggard position of the EU in global competition Re How to think about the EUs rescue fund Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: It is the brew that counts a lot
text: IT IS THE BREW THAT COUNTS A LOT Kicmelt temak In a veiy smart article FT argues for the valid tool of QE for emerging markets, especially for the middle-income countries using their own currencies /FT, 18 June 2020/. Indeed, we can benefit from the right monetaiy policies followed in the last decade, when we built up reserves and kept lending under control In Hungary, we reduced the central banks share in finance by shrinking the MNBs balance sheet from 40% to 25% of Hungarian GDP. It is absolutely right to warn us that quantitative easing should still be a last resort. We need a realty good mixture of conventional monetaiy policies, targeted means and quantitative easing to return to the convergence path of the 2010s. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central bank of Hungary Re Emerging markets can use quantitative easing, too

Title: It is the same, but different
text: IT IS THE SAME, BUT DIFFERENT Kicmelt temak That is for sure, Bidens 1.9 trillion-dollar stimulus is not only to kick start economic recoveiy in the American economy, but also a step to build up enough fire power to overcome unforeseen events in the future. /Gene Sperling, FT, 9 Februaiy 2021/ Last time, the US handled brilliantly the unfolding financial crisis in 10 months time. In 2008, there was a double-sword crisis to change guards in Washington and to launch an attack against the new emerging financial power, the euro area. This time it is the same, but different. Covidl9 resulted in the change of guards in Washington and the huge recoveiy chest boards are aiming for financing the warfare with China. However, this time it might take decades to conclude warfare, like in Europe between the 1630s and the 1650s. So, many more "recoveiy plans might follow suit. Title: It is wartime economics, but another kind
text: IT IS WARTIME ECONOMICS, BUT ANOTHER KIND Kicmelt temak In principle, both Lord Keynes and Lord Skidelsky are right: in a wartime economy and in times of supply lockdowns inflationary forces will be at large. But it is another kind of war than WW2 and most likely a V-shape crisis. It means that the previous deflationary path of the developed world will be back soon, as Gavyn Davies put it rightly /FT. 27 April 2020/. However, against all odds, inflation might be back next year, more likely in 2022, because we live in the time of the new 30 Years War. Wartime economics plays its part again in favor of higher inflation No one promised peaceful times when our relatives are the 1940s and the 1970s. Re Deflation threat from the virus will be long lasting' Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Italy needs a complete overhaul of taxation
text: ITALY NEEDS A COMPLETE OVERHAUL OF TAXAHON Kicmelt temak It is certainty true that Europes future, especially the euro areas future hinges on Italys reforms. /Andrea Lorenzo Capusella, FT, 27 April 2021/ Between 1995 and 2019, in a quarter of a centuiy, Italys productivity rose by a little more than quarter of the euro areas average and GDP per capita fell to 10 per cent below the euro area average from above 9 per cent. Undoubtedly, Italy needs sweeping structural reforms. Nevertheless, as we learnt it in Hungary, everything boils down to taxation We managed to introduce a new flat tax system, a restructured VAT regime, brand-new crisis taxes, a bank levy and the others. All of these resulted in a hugely successful fiscal consolidation in 18 months between the middle of 2010 and the end of 2011. All the achievements of the Hungarian economy in the 2010s originated from the early reform of taxation It is clear that Italy cannot hedge the issue called taxation Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re The EUs future hinges on Italys recovery fond reforms

Title: Italys unfinished business with the euro
text: ITALYS UNFINISHED BUSINESS WITH THE EURO Kicmelt temak On behalf of other European peers, Matteo Renzi broke up the Italian government, for the good. This time it is realty a historic opportunity for an Italian comeback. /FT Big Read, 10 Februaiy 2021/ Italy has been suffering from the euro area membership since the early years of the 2000s. Italian public debt exceeded 150% of GDP without any sign of a sustainable growth path or a national consensus for improving competitiveness. Last time the EU forced Mario Monti to launch brutal reforms without the badly needed financial resources. He foiled, Italy foiled and the euro area foiled. Now Italys time has come, parity because they have the right man to do the job. They have 200 billion euros to spend on reforms. We urge you to study the successful reforms of the V4 countries completed in the last decade. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re 'European politics

Title: Itinerary Congress of Economists - Presentation by Gyrgy Matolcsy
text: ITINERARY CONGRESS OF ECONOMISTS - PRESENTAHON BY GYORGY MATOLCSY Kicmelt temak Ladies and Gentlemen, There is a new world order, and a new world economy is forming within that. I would like to share some thoughts with you about the rules of this world economy. The rules are partly new, but some of them have been emerging since the advent of the internet in 1995-1996. This process was accelerated by the financial crisis in the US and Europe in 2007-2009, then by foe crisis in Greece and later in the euro area, and the application of the new rules of the world economy has gotten a huge boost by the pandemic. According to technology futurists, the implementation of the new rules in the global economy has jumped ahead by approximately ten years. I am not saying that this is a positive effect of the pandemic, but the present situation certainty does speed things up and act as a catalyst. Ladies and gentlemen, we have a difficult decade ahead of us. First, because of the pandemic, but also because we are living in a new world economy, with new rules. Hungarian sailor Zsombor Berecz showed how a fantastic athletic features, perseverance and skills help one clinch an Olympic silver medal And we can also win gold and bronze medals, as we showed the world at the Tokyo Games. The coming decade will be rough and turbulent, but we are in a quite favourable position at the outset. When compared to the Hungarian crisis in 2008-2009, the present situation differs in major aspects, and one of the biggest factors is the initial position. A little more than a decade ago, the Hungarian economy was in very bad shape when the crisis hit, and an internal crisis was exacerbated by an external one. Now, on the other hand, the calamity, or the series of calamities, hit the country after ten successful years. Let us see the recovery from the present complex crisis, which is a healthcare, economic, social, mental and emotional crisis but not a financial crisis. We can see that China, but also the US, have fared exceptionally weft Meanwhile, the euro area and the European Union have not been successful in crisis management. The OECD published its latest report yesterday, stating that the world economy has recovered from the crisis, reaching the levels seen at the end of 2019, and so did Hungary, which now moves in tandem with the mainstream of the global economy unlike the euro area and the European Union. The crisis and the rapid recovery have an extremely unpleasant and new side effect, namely the return of inflation. Inflation is a public enemy, and the central bank is required to fight it. The MNB has gone to battle to rein it in. However, it is not merely a Hungarian phenomenon, and not constrained to Europe. It can be observed all over the world: the fester the recovery, the greater the inflation figures. This is characteristic of every post-crisis recovery. There are reasons that lead to the emergence and acceleration of inflation. These include energy and commodity prices, the disruptions in supply chains, and excessive global liquidity, or money, in the world, which can also be seen in almost every country when we look at them individually. And of course, the impact of climate change, which should trigger a green transition, can also be traced in surging inflation. Crisis management has considerably bloated government debt the world over. This is due to budget deficits, even though the worlds central banks, every single one of them, took an active part in crisis management. It can also be observed that within the European Union, crisis management has become a sharp dividing line. 12-13 countries in the EuropeanUnion, about half of the Member States, have reached end-2019 GDP levels by the end of the second half of the year. Hungary is currently placed tenth, a quite impressive position, especially because it was ranked 15-16th in 2020. In 2021, some of the time lost in 2020 was made up, allowing the country to rise from the 15-16th place to the 1 Oth at the end of the second quarter this year. This is good, but I believe that there are major EuropeanUnion countries, for example Germany, France and Italy, where the end-2019 levels in the economy could not be restored by the end of the second quarter this year. This reflects an inefficient crisis management, unlike in countries, including Hungary, that have already restored earlier levels. It took Hungary six and a half years to recover from the American and European financial crisis of2007-2009, which appeared in Hungary in the autumn of2008, with its first signs felt in 2009, and return to the development and GDP per capita levels of2008. Very typically, and promisingly, this, ie. recovermg from the pandemic and the economic crisis triggered by the pandemic, now took the country about 15 months. Hungary performed a very rapid, V-shaped recovery, together with the nine other countries that have already reached end-2019 levels. Of course, the V-shaped rebound was not completed within a year. Ums was expected, but central bank experts only said that if no other wave comes in the pandemic and government projects start stoon, the complete recovery would probably be possible by the end of2020. This was thwarted by several factors, but in less than 18 months, Hungaiy performed a V-shaped recoveiy, returning to pre-crisis figures in terms of the level of development and GDP. How was this possible? One secret is that Hungaiy was Europes best in lending during the crisis. The 16.6% credit expansion in the household and business sectors placed Hungaiy on the top in Europe. In fact, the Hungarian crisis management had a lending focus, complemented with an investment-driven crisis management approach And loans have an important feature, as we all know from Istvan Szechenyi: they are actually trust materialised. By virtue of being driven by lending, Hungarian crisis management was based on trust and confidence. When looking at the extent to which the business sector, in particular micro, small and medium-sized enterprises used the opportunities offered by the FGS Go!, it is clear that those who do not believe that tomorrow will be better and that the pandemic measures will bear fruit, like some euro area countries, do not take out loans. On the other hand, those who are confident that their own countiy will be able to recover from the crisis, for instance based on the success in the past ten years, do take out loans. In other words, being first in Europe in terms of private sector lending and credit expansion means that Hungary was ranked first in preserving and even increasing confidence. This takes us to the Magyar Nemzeti Bank. When it comes to lending and money, one should definitely look at central bank programmes. It can be seen that the Magyar Nemzeti Bank provided Hungary with over HUF 10 billion for crisis management. The structure of this assistance shows that the orchestra of the central bank played a variety of tunes and instruments at the same time, and almost all elements were precisely targeted. There were components that helped target targeting, for example under FGS Go! working capital loans affected the source of wages, as micro, small and medium-sized enterprises took out most loans for preserving wages and the headcount. And this is confidence all over again Firms retained workers because they trusted the future, and they took out loans because they were confident that they would recover their strength, sales revenue and profit figures in the years to come. And every instrument was successful I would like to highlight the FGS Go!, and offer you a behind-the-scenes look at its birth. When the management of the Ministiy for National Economy heard that the minister and many managers would switch to the Magyar Nemzeti Bank in the spring of 2013, we started to think about what we would do once we got there. We knew that we would be working with fabulous experts. But we also knew that the central bank was a closed gold mine, to put it mildly, in other words it did not function as it was supposed to. As March 2013 neared, we found a small cafe, chose its most secluded comer, and developed the Funding for Growth Scheme, a targeted economic stimulus package, with four or five of my colleagues. We already knew that the banking system required a zero-per cent loan The banks had to be used, and the barking system was our greatest ally. It was clear, right from the outset, that the interest on the loans cannot be higher than 2.5%, that the loans should be given to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and all the other basic aspects were also straightforward. At the central bank, we met highly skilled professionals, and I asked them how this would work. They immediately showed me a programme, the Funding for Landing programme of the Bank of England, which was a bit different, but we could claim in Brussels and Frankfurt that there had already been a precedent for such a solution When Hungary was in trouble in 2020-2021, and it still is, because the pandemic persists, it was able to use an instrument that had originally been devised for another ailment. When the Funding for Growth Scheme was introduced in June 2013, the outstanding credit of micro, small and medium- sized enterprises had been diminishing by 510 per cent for four years, leading to a credit crunch. The FGS was the perfect tool to address this, and it was just as successful in a different situation as today. If we need to list the largest differences between the crisis management of2008-2009 and today, we should definitely say that the initial position was completely different this time round. Now, problems need to be addressed in a solid country that is in excellent economic health. The other difference is that back then the central bank balance sheet could not be opened up for crisis management. One should only consider what HUF 1, 2 or 5 billion would have meant in 2010-2012, in the crisis management at that time. But in those days the central bank was in no position to open up its balance sheet. This required fiscal consolidation in the first place. And the base rate of 7% did not help either. The second major difference between the two crisis management situations is that the Hungarian central bank was now able to open up its balance sheet and find the instruments that managed the crisis in a targeted manner, rather than just pump money into the economy. Dear congress leaders, I believe it is a huge achievement that while during the crisis management of2008-2009 employment continued to decline, with 200,000 jobs lost, now only 50,00(-l00,000 jobs were terminated temporarily, but by the end of the second quarter of this year, the earlier, very favourable employment levels returned. This is another huge difference between the crisis management situations, and this is also due to confidence. Entrepreneurs cannot save or recreate jobs if they do not trust the future. Confidence is die real driver behind preserving, or even raising, employment levels. That is the starting point. But what will the rules and new trends in the new world order look like? There are four main paths leading into the future. These include the digital, the green and the creative paths, culminating in the rise of Eurasia. If the trends are transposed onto a fusion map, this is more or less what we see until 2030. Here, it has to be emphasised again that the complex crisis has accelerated all trends pointing towards the future, in particular the digitalisation and technology change trends as well as the trends of accumulating knowledge capital The knowledge capital that is generated in this phase is different from earlier versions. The crisis also accelerates the utilisation of talents. The world was forced to jump ahead ten years due to the crisis. In every economic period that involves a change of paradigm, just like the one we are experiencing today, new megatrends are born. We have identified 12 megatrends. Their germs were already present in the world economy in 1995-1996 and then after 2008-2009, but now their emergence has accelerated. Every megatrend has become fester and stronger, exerting a greater impact. They include digitalisation and the contactless economy as well as the revolution of money. There are hardly any central banks in the world that do not think about introducing a central bank digital currency. The transition to the green economy has turned from a strange fed into a mainstream idea. Platforms and the data-based economy are reinforced, just like the regionalisation trend. A new world order is emerging, which is in constant interaction with the new rules of the world economy. We still do not know whether they only have a positive effect on each other, or they exert a strong negative impact, too, for example through the disruption of supply and production chains. What is certain, however, is that the emergence of the new world order has gained momentum. The tech giants and technology itself has benefited enormously from the crisis. Services have entered a new stage, shifting away from the personal towards file indirect. Our homes have become not only kinder and safer, but also a key space for work and all file related activities, such as learning and expanding knowledge. All forms of security have become more important, and they include health security and financial or market balance, which refers to the balance between supply and demand, in other words keeping inflation in check. Fortunately, leading a healthy lifestyle has also become significant more important. It has become clear that greater havoc can be caused where health is already unstable due to something. And of course, the world of work is also being profoundly transformed. The new economic world order and the new rules are all digital It is now realty high time for increasingly using robots in the world, and there is a green revolution under way. I think everyone feels the truth in the old saying that the middleman is dead. Direct relationships are coming, without the need for middlemen This is becoming widespread in all economic fields, and our consumer habits are changing. I believe that every healthy product and service and safe consumption are becoming more important, and there is going to be a boom in this in file future. There is an ongoing digital revolution of money, progressing at breakneck speed, and we are living in the age of big data, large databanks and the transformation of information into data. The economy is being based on data, although Hungaiy lags behind in this respect. The utilisation of the wealth of (public) data is currently veiy low in the country, with Hungaiy bringing ip the rear in the European Union in this respect, whereas successful countries are ranked in the top three or five. A data revolution or reforms are needed, which calls for a state or government programme, and of course the central bank and the financial system will also be willing to help in eveiy such government measure. Financial innovations are accelerating. At the central bank, we refer to this as the revolution of money. There is a greater state presence, so this is not the age of private money: the state will play a greater role in the world of money fundamental transformed and revolutionised by technologies. This can already be seen in China, and I believe that it is already happening in the West, albeit under the surface for now. And just as the role and more efficient functioning of the state have become crucial in this new age, for example due to crises, the interest of the state, or the public, will be essential in the revolution of money. Access to money will be key, in particular providing many people with easy, cheap, fest and secure access to loans and all types of funds. There are actually two types of countries. Ones where leaders and central banks can make firm decisions, and those where decisions are made less promptly. Just as in managing the crisis and the pandemic, the winners of the revolution of money will be those who are determined and able to make tough and difficult decisions in a snap. Ladies and gentlemen, hybrid financial systems are emerging. We first saw this in the car industry, but we are already seeing it in the union of labour and robots, in most of manufecturing. And the same goes for the financial system New forms of money creation are coming. Competitiveness, lending incentives and capital and capital flows are gaining importance. We foresee the transformation of the banking system until 2030. This is important because in a hybrid financial system the existing financial system is retained but transformed while it becomes fester, and it is complemented by, through fusion, with a financial system based on new technologies. Digital payments are accelerating. Hungary leads the pack with the introduction of the instant payment system In feet, the country is in a very special position because the whole economy and financial system transitioned to the instant payment system, at the behest of a central force, the central bank. Elsewhere this has caused more trouble because it was sought to be introduced on a voluntary basis. Well, in this case central regulation was better. Everyone partic ipates in online sales in some form With respect to the growth of online sales in Hungary during the crisis of2020-2021, the country has definitely jumped ahead by at least ten years in 12-18 months. Hungary lagged fer behind in online sales, and it is now placed in the top three international. And this is only the beginning of e-commerce. I believe that the American and Chinese technology companies, the Big Tech, are the big winners of the crisis. For example the five largest technology firms in the US increased their assets and market capitalisation by USD 2 trillion in the first months of the crisis. Well, this continues, and those with a strong technology barrel ahead and win, and those with mediocre technology drop out. The technological revolution is driven by software, hardware and chip manufecturing. But this list will shortly be expanded with many other things. Examples include artificial intelligence, augmented reality, cyber and quantum technologies, deepwater technologies and other military technologies that economists are fortunately unfamiliar with. But what is already clear is that the winners will be those who are able to develop the most efficient technologies or put their hands on them fest. That is why the Hungarian economic strategy and the strategy of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade that implements it are excellent, as they focus on obtaining the most advanced technologies from the world, mostly from Asia and the US. As a result of the crisis, the winners will be those who use technology in manufecturing and all other walks of life. Robotisation first appeared in manufecturing but it is quickly spreading to all fecets of our lives. Actually, a hybrid economy is on the rise, a fusion between manual labour and robots and later also artificial intelligence. In this area too, the winners will be those who put robots to use in all areas of life. Many activities are transferred to our homes. We will work out and do yoga with our children We will bake bread and produce many things at home. The home will become a space of fusions, concentrating family life, work, learning, knowledge accumulation and several other things. That is why the success of the Green Home Programme just launched by the Hungarian central bank is so important. I think everyone is aware that a sharing and platform economy is on the rise, as economic, pandemic and social crises speed up the spread of the sharing economy. This is what triggers the calls for a green transition and a sustainable economy and also social sustainability. One of the social effects of the crisis has been the considerable growth of income and wealth inequalities. And social balance and stability are crucial for any kind of economic performance. The sharing economy is a response to the growing wealth and income inequalities, offering the help of technology to states and governments and society. The internet allows us to access the worlds knowledge at almost no cost. The price of basic economic resources tends towards zero. This is obvious when it comes to the real price of information, money and energy. And the sharing economy offers us a cheaper, better, fester and more accessible life. The new rules of the world economy and the transition are green Green is also a catchword for all things sustainable. The economy, society, governments, central banks and eveiything else in the future need to be sustainable. We can clearly see that the green idea, the idea of sustainability, has progressed at least ten years due to the crisis. At present, this can also be observed in the government debt and budget deficit in the developed world, but we will return to the idea that financial balance is important at lightning speed, within a few years. But the green transition is just as important in the energy system, the vehicle industry, the financial system and eveiy other area. Hungaiy has broadly foe same opportunities as the rest of the world. The green transition can be implemented and accelerated through investments. New technologies need to be involved, and sustainable solutions create new jobs. This helps in establishing a society transitioning to a healthier lifestyle. Financial innovations also hold a huge green potential, one only needs to think of the loans in the Green Home Programme. Of course, the challenges are also huge. I believe that Hungaiy is well placed to take advantage of all the opportunities, increasingly dynamically, and manage the challenges. The transition depends on making firm decisions, just like in the case of the other post-pandemic trends. If the state can lead the way and make the most important decisions, a good position can be achieved, just as with the management of the pandemic and the economic crisis. Therefore I think that taking advantage of the opportunities is of utmost importance. I believe many people can already sense that the Magyar Nemzeti Bank is one of the first among central banks, and the first in many cases, in calling for and financing a green transition Thanks to the approval of the European Central Bank and the decision of the Hungarian parliament, the central bank received a green mandate, which is utilised. The Magyar Nemzeti Bank is the first central bank in the world to use its opportunity to speed up the green transition thanks to its mandate. Our green programme covers capital markets and the banking system as a whole. We stimulate the banking system and the property market with small, often invisible but effective instruments to perform a green transition, and the Magyar Nemzeti Bank also offsets its own ecological footprint. Be the change, as many people have said. And yes, the Magyar Nemzeti Bank embodies change, and we continue to advocate and encourage this in the entire financial system Ladies and gentlemen, the new world is creative, and new rules pointing towards creativity apply. Economist Sandor Kopacsi has taught us that talent, knowledge and capital are all veiy important. He added to this list the natural environment. We expanded this system a bit with technology, which also plays an important role. Actually, we are experiencing the fusion of four (two times two) fectors, and this was accelerated by the pandemic. Knowledge, talent, technology and capital were already interconnected, but now those who do not link them and create fusions between these four fectors cannot win Those who do not use this four-fector fusion for a green transition and for creating a sustainable society, will also lose out. There will be both winners and losers. It is clear that the countries, cities, companies and femilies that learn to share machines and platforms will be the winners. This is hybrid world and a hybrid economy where manual labour and technology not only exist side by side, but they coexist in fusion The creative industry plays an increasingly important role in this. Now the global music industry and streaming companies exhibit this growing importance. But whenever there is talent involved in an idea and then in the product or service, things are becoming important. Because creativity is both talent and skill The green and sustainable transition requires a high investment rate, which is a precondition for the new rules of the world economy. Therefore Hungary needs to increase investment into the so-called e-material resources. The winners will be able to make knowledge, intellectual goods, creativity and talent count more through investments. The way we do work will be transformed, as we can see it, also in our own lives. The healthy lifestyle is also clearly becoming more important. Let me make a personal comment here: currently the greatest obstacle to Hungarys successful sustainable convergence is the overall health of the Hungarian society. This is mostly due to the attitude to our own health. We need to transition to a healthy, health- focused thinking and lifestyle, which was accelerated considerably by the pandemic. This is vital for Hungarys success. The idea that we will become healthier and think differently when we become rich is flawed. No, we will become rich if we change the way we think about our health. We need a completely different health industry, and we have to put health in the focus. We are at the stage of Eurasias rise, and that region is perhaps the greatest buffer zone of the new world order. Yet, when considering the rules of the economy, it is clear that the US and China are the two major players. If we also look at the 1.4 billion people in China, we can see that it is still a developing country. It is a very poor country in several respects, so its rivalry with the United States is like David fighting Goliath. At any rate, a new phase based on a dual world order is expected in geopolitics and of course in the world economy. Eurasia as a continent will become interconnected starting out from China. 40,000 years ago, Europe and Asia were a unified continent in terms of music, trade and religions, and we are now once again headed towards more homogeneity. But this will be a long process. Europe is in trouble, in many ways, according to Americans. Europe is in trouble because it cannot make decisions, it is hesitant and fragmented, and it wants to build an empire but it is not suitable for that at all How much Europe is in trouble can be seen in its underdog position in the market of global tech giants. Europe currently stands to lose in the technological competition, but this will hopefully change. That is why I have praised Hungarys strategy, which states that if we cannot import advanced technologies from Europe, let us turn towards Asia and the US. Global trade will change course, and this process already started in 2009. According to an excellent analysis, the age of weightless or immaterial globalisation is coming, referring to the globalisation of data and intellectual goods, and the globalisation that characterised the previous world order and world economy is now over. Security is becoming more important, so a profit-oriented operation is partly shifting towards security-conscious operation. This requires a new economic theory and thinking. At the central bank we say that economic theory needs to be reformed, and a paradigm shift is necessary. We will discuss this in detail in the near future, dedicating a book to the subject. But it is already clear that these transitions can only be accelerated if our thinking changes, because in the beginning there was the Word, so everything started with the mind and ideas, which produce reality. Ladies and gentlemen, Hungary has tackled the calamity after ten successful years, and we are in a very good position at the beginning of the new race, during which the new world opens up, and we will continue to pick up speed as we press ahead. Thank you for your attention.

Title: Just at the dawn of a new period
text: JUST AT THE DAWN OF A NEW PERIOD Kicmelt temak The Plaza Accord closed a long period between 1971 and 1985, when the US ended the former global financial order based on the Bretton Woods Agreement /1971/ and shifted the main anchor of global finance from gold to oil The new golden rule was the constant ratio between the price of gold and oil, instead of the dollar and gold. Oil seems to be out of the game now, information/data are stepping in, China and the renminbi replace Japan and the yen as Mansoor Mohi-uddin rightly put it. /FT, 2 October 2020/ However, we are just at the beginning of a long journey leading to a new Plaza Accord. We are still one year away from 1971. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Renminbi strength foretells dollars decline

Title: Learn from the 2020 GDP data
text: LEARN FROM THE 2020 GDP DATA Kiemelt temak A professor of political arithmetic urges us to scrap 2020 GDP data regarding it as totally useless. /Daniel Miigge, FT, 4 Januaiy/ Not at all, instead let us leam a lot from2020. For sure, the west failed to handle any of the three crisis -pandemic, fear, economic loss - efficiently. Asia fared much better. Both individuals and governments handled all sort of crisis better in Asia, than in Europe or in the U.S. One of the culprits is Western liberal thinking where individual freedom is above all other values. In Asia, common good trumps all other values. Another is the perception of time. Western thinking tends to be short-sighted, Eastern horizon tends to be much longer. Hence, Western crisis management focused on safeguarding incomes, Asians concentrated on launching investments. Digital and green transition, electrification, robotics and all other disruptive technologies gained momentum via the pandemic in Asia. The west tries to save the present, ie. the past, in the meantime, the east aims for winning the future. No wonder... Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Scrap 2020 GDP data to find a path out of the harm done by coronavirus

Title: Live and let live
text: LIVE AND LET LIVE Kicmelt temak Metus hostilis /fear of the enemy/ is always the deepest trigger for governments policies in all countries at all times, especially for the American Empire /Janan Ganesh, FT, 17 Februaiy 2021/. When it comes to the U.S., indeed, wars had been forging the ever-larger and stronger world power. Nevertheless, you need two different strategies for building up and maintaining an empire. Wars proved to be instrumental to create the empire, but they can be detrimental to it when you are on the top. Instead, youd better use the other major piece of Roman advice to avoid a major war. The policy ofDivide et impera is definitely better than waging a risky war. Besides, empires and world powers finally vanished, but some smart nations survived. The ancient recipe for survival is to live and let live. Re Americas best hope of hanging together is China

Title: A basic personal equity and loan programme for all
text: MATOLCSY: A BASIC PERSONAL EQUITY AND LOAN PROGRAMME FOR ALL Kiemelt temak Monica de Bolle is right in more than one way /FT, 19 May 2020/, but why should we stick to former ideas when we can find much more promising opportunities for all citizens in both the developed and developing worlds. Anyway, rich and poor live together in both worlds. What if we offer land to all individuals and families as equity for housing and business? Why dont we offer ownership in commercial and industrial districts for would-be small and medium sized entrepreneurs? Why dont we distribute computers and software for families and future employees freely? In the aftermath of the Covid-19 pandemic, working from home-office, virtual reality/distancing, digital transformation or using 4.0/5.0 industrial products will be accelerated. Title: A long-lasting tragedy of the euro zone
text: MATOLCSY: A LONG-LASTING TRAGEDY OF THE EURO ZONE Kicmelt temak It was long overdue to spot the substance of the past 20 years of the euro, Martin Wolf did it /FT, October 29 2019/. Yes, a tragedy of the euro zone, especially of Germanys role within it, is that the transition to thinking about how income and expenditure add up at euro zone and global levels has so far failed to occur. Title: AI and oil
text: MATOLCSY: Al AND OIL Kicmclt temak Wolfgang Miinchau rightly points at some reasons why the EU has been lagging behind the US and China in Al patent filings, Al investments - simply in all areas of the new Al era /FT, 24 Februaiy 2020/. Western Europe had no oil - apart from Scotland and Norway - in the long petrodollar era between the 1970s and the 2020s. Title: Another sort of U-turn is needed
text: MATOLCSY: ANOTHER SORT OF U-TURN IS NEEDED Kicmelt temak I completely disagree with Melvyn Krauss, who says that the southern countries in the euro area should shrink their global exports by increasing their intra-EU trade towards the northern euro zone economies. /FT, 22 October 2020/ It would be detrimental to their future role in the global economy cementing the present laggard position of the southern belt of the euro zone in competitiveness, investment, and high-tech exports. It would also diminish the overall EU position in global trade, competitiveness and investment by further weakening the already weak half of the European currency area. Instead, they should launch sweeping structural reforms in taxation, finance, education and at the labour market in order to enhance their global and intra-EU competitiveness. Also, they should celebrate the 30th anniversary of the Maastricht Treaty by initiating a complete overhaul of the euro in 2022. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re More intra-EU trade can counter US on currencies

Title: Appearances can be deceptive
text: MATOLCSY: APPEARANCES CAN BE DECEPTIVE Kicmelt temak Janan Ganesh is definitely right in telling us that Americas internal schisms are being used against it /FT, 4 June 2020/. Title: Appearances can be deceptive
text: MATOLCSY: APPEARANCES CAN BE DECEPTIVE Kicmelt temak Columnist Charlemagne fell in the trap of wishful thinking /Charlemagne, The Economist, February 15th 2020/. Europe has no chance to become boring again In the 2020s, the EU will have to face all the hard consequences of mistakes made in previous decades. The unsolved structural problems of the euro, migration, the wrongdoings of the German car industry, the rifts between Northern and Southern members, the divisions between Western and Eastern countries, the deterioration in industrial competitiveness of the core economies of the EU - just to name some of them- will stubbornly haunt us for years. Title: Asians in the European Union
text: MATOLCSY: ASIANS IN THE EUROPEAN UNION Kiemelt temak Ruchir Shanna is right that the present hotspot of the global economy is in eastern Europe. /FT, 13 September 3021/ The three larger economies - Poland, Hungary and Romania- are veiy close to the advanced level set by the IMF /an above per capita income 17 000 US dollars/. This looming regional success stoiy seems to repeat the former achievements of the Asian tigers and some outstanding Chinese megacities. The pattern is similar to all of them With the help of a highly educated and skilled workforce they realty found the proven key to long-term growth: manufacturing prowess. Besides, they form a regional cluster, as did all the tigers and dragons in east Asia. They are veiy close to the strongest European economy Germany, meaning that they take part in globalization via the German export machine. However, it is always challenging to have more good decades after a successful one /Hungary/, or two /Romania/ or even three /Poland/. This is the veiy reason why we badly need new structural reforms focusing on competitiveness and building efficient institutions. Title: Capitalism will be more different than it was before
text: MATOLCSY: CAPITALISM WILL BE MORE DIFFERENT THAN IT WAS BEFORE Kicmelt temak John Thornhill seemingly deals with billionaires of three continents, but in feet he deals with three different types of capitalism in America, Europe and China/FT, 26 May 2020/. In my view, Europe will not become more American in terms of wealth creation, just as the US will not become more European All the key sources of wealth creation - disruptive new technologies, the size of domestic markets, die depth of stock exchanges and government regulations - will be more different in the future for the three economies than they are now. Continents of capitalism will not come closer to each other, on the contraiy, the gap between them will be even larger in the 2020s. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re The changing face of the billionaire classes

Title: CBDC will ease the pressure of inflation in the 2020s
text: MATOLCSY: CBDC WILL EASE THE PRESSURE OF INFLAHON IN THE 2020S Kicmelt temak Digital cash will make inflation worse, so central banks should slow down their space race to offcr digital currencies until after price pressures ease /Andy Mukheriee, Bloomberg, Economics, 5/17/2021/. Realty? First of all, there is no such a thing than a space race offering digital currencies. Just the opposite, there are extremely cautious virtual and practical experiments that might lead to digital cash Like in other areas of the global economy, we are on the right track to create hybrid systems using an accelerated transition process from the old to the new worlds. Who promised that all players would be able to convert all the funds in their bank accounts into electronic cash issued directly by a monetaiy authority? Instead of an automatic conversion, banks should be able to use electronic cash to finance the transition to a green, digital and sustainable economic structure of the future. They will be able to create completely new economic areas via investments funded by digital currencies. It means, by definition, that they will enhance the supply side of our economies and this would ease the inflation pressures of the 2020s. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Can digital cash make inflation worse?

Title: Central bankers can and should remain risk-averse investors
text: MATOLCSY: CENTRAL BANKERS CAN AND SHOULD REMAIN RISK-AVERSE INVESTORS Kicmelt temak Pressure of low returns is forcing some reserve managers of some central banks to take on greater risk to preserve their capital /Tommy Stubbington, FT, Central banks, 5/17/2021/. They should not do that by seeking out riskier assets for reserves, and they still can have safe assets for their higher reserves. As for taking greater risk, having the big picture of a nation there is no greater risk than jeopardizing the stability of the central bank. Especially the central banks of emerging economies should park their reserves in safe assets such as government debts and gold in order to keep their currencies steady and protect them in times of crisis. Besides, the long yield drought seems to be coming to an end, so reserve managers can avoid the risk-trap. Also, they can find a good enough mixture of short-term and long-term government debts. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Central banks seek out riskier assets for reserves in yield drought

Title: Central bankers need optimism to restore trust
text: MATOLCSY: CENTRAL BANKERS NEED OPTIMISM TO RESTORE TRUST Kicmelt temak There are no small or large central banks these days, there are only rightly optimistic or wrong!/ pessimistic ones. The first can restore trust in the global and national economies. The latter can only make things worse by deepening a vicious circle instead of igniting a virtuous circle in our financial comrnunities. The PBOC belongs to the first by telling us that the contagion has exerted a downward pressure on Chinas economy, but it will not last long /Chen Yulu, FT, 21 Februaiy 2020/. The deputy governor is absolutely right, this brave and reliable message should be heard in the whole global village. We Hungarians fully share this view, a quick V-shape will unfold in the majority of the global economy, where optimism can defeat pessimism. Re Chinas central bank will help the economy rebound quickly Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Central bankers should talk less
text: MATOLCSY: CENTRAL BANKERS SHOULD TALK LESS Kicmelt temak Free exchange put a question mark behind the text /The Economist, October 26th 2019/. It was not needed. We should talk less, due to some hidden elements of central bankers lives. We cannot talk about substance. We are not eligible to touch upon politics, taxation, exchange rates, the flaws of inflation targeting, demography or poverty. We cannot talk about our human nature, emotions, values, family - it would be considered unprofessional. We are also not allowed to talk seriously about the future. Central bankers are regarded much more influential than they are; talking about the future would be too much We can be green, as all of us should be. Re A little less conversation Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Central banks have major roles in tackling climate change
text: MATOLCSY: CENTRAL BANKS HAVE MAJOR ROLES IN TACKLING CLIMATE CHANGE Kicmelt temak There are opposite sides in the debate on central banks role in tackling climate change /Rachael King, Central Banking, 6/9/2021/. Some argue for an active role others fear of overreach It is, however, not the question of either/or, it is the question of survival or disaster. It is also the matter of missing the creation of the new economy or grasping it. It is not a peaceful and comfortable transition from the old, unsustainable economic order to the new sustainable one, it is the war for the future. Recalling the wise words of Montecuccoli, it is clear-cut that winning wars need money, money and money. All forms of money and financial institutions will be needed to finance an accelerated transition. We need green credits, green grants, green digital cash, greenish commercial and investment banks, green Regulators, a green fintech sector and many more. The green - and digital- transition will be the new engine for creating growth, jobs, wealth and quality living standards. All these will result in a completely new economy. All in all, this ongoing global war must be financed, regulated and accelerated by central banks. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Policy-makers debate central banks role in tackling climate change

Title: Central banks never run out of bullets
text: MATOLCSY: CENTRAL BANKS NEVER RUN OUT OF BULLETS Kicmelt temak Nouriel Roubini is certainty right telling us that much more negative rates are not realty viable for the ECB /Markets Insight, FT, 26 Februaiy 2020/. However, this does not mean that central banks will run out of bullets. Hungary became the fallen angel of the EU by 2010. Since then, both the government and the central bank have been using unconventional and targeted means to turn the economy around. These policies resulted in the most efficient crisis management within the EU between 2010 and 2012, and one of the best macroeconomic performances between 2013 and 2019. Concerted eflbrts and targeted policies can make economic wonders. Re Investors remain complacent about virus despite sell-off Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary

Title: Chinas Covid pride is well deserved
text: MATOLCSY: CHINAS COVID PRIDE IS WELL DESERVED Kicmelt temak Dont hedge the issue, instead lets face the truth. The Chinese government realty has done a much better job in containing the disease than the US and the EU. China will be the only G20 economy to expand in 2020. This is exactly the veiy reason why international sentiment finally has not eroded towards China, contraiy to what Gideon Rachman suggests. /FT, 27 October/ China does not want to export the so called China model; however, western countries always tiy to export their liberal democracies to all the other menbers of the global community. Nevertheless, all western countries -liberal democracies and others - failed in handling the pandemic as efficiently as nearly all Asian countries. It is not the model, it is the mindset of the people that mattered most in success or failure. In the west, we should be more Chinese, Japanese, Koreans, Singaporeans and Asians in the run up to the next crisis/pandemics of the 2020s. Governor Matolcsy, MNB, the Central Bank of Hungary Re Chinas Covid triumphalism could be premature

Title: Chinas investment-led strategy is right
